A Markdown clip is ingested from its own body; its source: (or url:) frontmatter becomes the source URL, title: its title and kind: (article, paper, email or video) its kind. Every URL the worker fetches itself is checked first: only http(s), only public addresses, on every redirect.

docs.title: Add a link
docs.text:
sb add https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten

Queued 1 (0 already known). `sb run` processes them.

Nothing is downloaded yet. Add as many as you like in one command: sb add URL1 URL2 URL3. Put a link that has ? or & in quotes, or the shell reads it: sb add "https://example.com/post?id=7". Then:

sb run

To do one right now, without the queue, use sb ingest URL (add --dry-run to print the model's plan and write nothing). A page that needs a login, or is mostly scripts, fails with No readable article content found: clip it with the Web Clipper instead. A GitHub repository link is read through its README.

docs.title: Add a PDF
docs.text:
Either copy it into the vault's inbox/ folder and scan:

cp ~/Downloads/paper.pdf ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/inbox/

sb scan

Queued 1 sources from the inbox.

or give its path to sb add, which leaves the file where it is:

sb add ~/Downloads/paper.pdf

The difference: a file in inbox/ is moved to raw/inbox/, which keeps it for good. A file added by path is read from where it is when the run starts, so do not move it before then. Either way a copy of the PDF is saved in raw/ when the note is written. sb run scans inbox/ itself, so sb scan is only for seeing the queue early.

How the text of a PDF is read. The text is rebuilt from the characters in the PDF's text layer (with PDFium, the PDF engine of Chrome), as plain Markdown: lines are joined into paragraphs, a hyphen at the end of a line is dropped inside a word and kept in a compound (feed-forward), running headers and page numbers are dropped, and headings are found by font size, weight and numbering (## 1 Introduction, ### 3.1 Method; a file keeps at most 8 per page, at least 40, the numbered and the biggest first). Three things to know:

  • Tables are not Markdown tables. Each row stays on one line with its numbers intact (Base 65 27.3 3.3), so the model can read the values but the note does not show a grid.
  • Text inside images and charts is not read. Text printed over a picture, and the labels of a chart (a label that the file repeats 8 times or more, and short lines packed into one spot of a page), are left out of the text (a scanned PDF is the exception: with OCR its pages are read as images).
  • Figures are the embedded pictures and, when a drawing has a Figure N caption next to it, that vector drawing too (diagrams and flow charts); the panels under one caption count as one figure; at most 8 per PDF, rendered at a bounded size.

A PDF that needs a password is rejected with Could not open PDF: .... The notes keep emphasis out of the text (no ** or _x_), which is why a quote copied from it matches the PDF word for word more often. Why it is built this way, and what it cannot do: How a note is made.

How a PDF's note gets its title. The title stored in the PDF (its metadata Title) is used only when the first two pages show it, because a slide deck often keeps the title of the template it was made from. Otherwise the note is named after the file: _ reads as a space, so does - in a name with no spaces (spacing-effect.pdf), extra spaces are dropped, and the .pptx, .docx, .key or .odp that an export leaves (Slides.pptx.pdf) is removed. Notes made before 0.4.0 keep their names: rename one in Obsidian, which updates the links to it.

docs.title: Add a folder of PDFs
docs.text:
Let the shell list the files:

sb add ~/Papers/*.pdf

Queued 2 (0 already known). `sb run` processes them.

If the PDFs are in subfolders, copy them all into inbox/ first:

find ~/Papers -name '*.pdf' -exec cp {} ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/inbox/ \;

Two different files with the same name would overwrite each other during the copy (the worker only protects files after they reach inbox/). The worker skips a PDF it already has (same bytes, even under another name) and keeps a different PDF with the same name as name (2).pdf. A big folder takes a long time with a local model: sb run --limit 5 processes five at a time, and the nightly job does batches of 20 (max_sources_per_run), up to 6 a day (max_batches_per_day).

docs.title: Add a Markdown clip
docs.text:
A clip is a Markdown file with title: and source: (the page URL) at the top. The Web Clipper makes them; so can any tool that saves a page as Markdown.

---
title: Notes on the spacing effect
source: https://example.org/spacing
kind: article
---

The spacing effect says that learning is better when study sessions are spread out...

Drop it in inbox/ (or sb add clip.md). The text of the file is the source; the page is not fetched again. A clip with fewer than 40 characters of text is rejected as empty. Setting the Clipper up: Web Clipper and YouTube.

Page chrome is removed first. A clip of a GitHub, LinkedIn, X (Twitter), Reddit or YouTube page carries the site's own furniture along with the text: menus, "Sign in", cookie and consent lines, GitHub's repository sidebar (Languages, Releases, Contributors), reaction and share bars, "People also viewed", related-post lists, footers. The worker removes the lines it knows to be that furniture before the model reads the clip, so the note is about the article and not about the menu. The rule is conservative on purpose:

  • Only a whole line goes, and only when the whole line is known chrome; a sentence that merely contains such words is kept, and so are code blocks, plain bullets and YouTube transcript rows.
  • The site is known from the clip's source: address. Without one, the page's own footer text identifies it. A clip from any other site is left exactly as it is.
  • The original clip stays in raw/inbox/ untouched. A clip dropped in inbox/ is moved there; a clip you add by path from anywhere else (sb add clip.md, sb ingest clip.md) is copied there, unchanged, when its note is written (a taken name becomes name (2).md: nothing in raw/ is overwritten, and a copy that is already there is not made again). The snapshot raw/<date>-<slug>.md, which is what the note was made from, holds the stripped text.
  • The note records how many lines went as stripped_lines: N in its frontmatter (only when N is more than 0), and the run prints a warning: Removed N lines of page chrome from the clip.
  • The 40-character minimum is applied after stripping, so a clip that was only chrome (a login wall, a cookie page) is rejected with has almost no text.

docs.title: Add a YouTube video
docs.text:
Clip the video page with the Web Clipper's YouTube template: it needs a video that has a transcript, and it is described in Web Clipper and YouTube. The note is written from the transcript, and quotes and glossary terms get a link that opens the video at that second. The worker never downloads video or audio.

Without the Clipper, a file with kind: video, source: set to the video's URL and a transcript with one line per row, each written as **2:20** · text of the line, is read the same way.

docs.title: Add an image or a scanned PDF
docs.text:
This needs OCR turned on once (below). Then it is the same as a PDF:

sb add ~/Pictures/slide.png

Queued 1 (0 already known). `sb run` processes them.

Without OCR, sb add says why instead of queueing:

error: not an http(s) URL or an existing .pdf/.md file:
  ~/Pictures/slide.png
  Images: add an [llm.ocr] model to config.toml to read images and scanned PDFs (`sb init --ocr`, docs/reference/configuration.md)

docs.title: Add an email
docs.text: Set up the mailbox once (sb setup email); after that, forward anything to your you+esbi-cli@gmail.com address and the next sb run makes a note. See Capture email.

docs.title: Import an older vault
docs.text:
If you have an older folder of links and PDFs (Links/DD-MM-YYYY.md with one [url] per line, and PDFs/), set legacy_vault under [paths] in the config and run it once:

sb import-legacy

Queued 5 sources (0 already known).

It never changes the old folder, and is safe to repeat.

docs.title: Images and scanned PDFs (OCR)
docs.text:
Off by default, and a choice you can make, see and change. See where you stand:

sb ocr status

Turn it on, and have the model downloaded now:

sb ocr enable --pull

(sb init asks the same question the first time, default No; sb init --ocr [--ocr-model NAME] [--pull-ocr-model] does it without questions. Nothing is downloaded without --pull, a typed yes, or ollama pull by hand.) The recommended model is qwen3-vl:2b-instruct:

ollama pull qwen3-vl:2b-instruct     # 1.9 GB download, about 3.4 GB in memory while it reads

sb ocr disable turns it off and keeps the model choice (the same as enabled = false under [llm.ocr]). deepseek-ocr:3b is a choice for machines with 16 GB of memory or more; on an 8 GB Mac it is far too slow: see Choosing the OCR model.

A vision model served by Ollama on your machine reads the text printed in the image, and that text becomes the source: the note is made like any other (summary, glossary, quotes checked against the text). The original image is kept in raw/ and shown in the note under "Figuras".

  • What it reads well: screenshots, slides, and pages of text, in English and Spanish, including a photo taken at a slight angle with some noise. Measured numbers are in Choosing the OCR model.
  • What it cannot do: a photo or a diagram with no text has nothing to read. The source then fails with no readable text, and the reason is kept in the queue (sb status); no empty note is written. It does not describe pictures, because a description is the model's guess and none of it can be checked against the source. It does not read handwriting reliably, and it can drop or swap a word in dense small print: check anything that matters against the original.
  • Scanned PDFs: a PDF whose pages have no text layer is rendered page by page and read the same way. At most [run].ocr_max_pages pages (default 10) are read; when a PDF is longer the run says how many were read.
  • Time: expect from a few seconds (a screenshot) to under a minute per page on a small Mac, since the reading model and the writing model take turns in Ollama.
  • Private by construction: the OCR model must be an Ollama model running on this machine ([llm.ocr] refuses anything else), so an image, and the text read from it, is never sent to a cloud model. If a scanned PDF or an image came attached to an email, the text read from it is treated as email (only your local [llm.private] model writes it).
  • Not supported (reported by sb scan and sb run, never ignored): HEIC (convert it to JPG first), Word, and any other file type. They stay in inbox/.

docs.title: If a source already exists
docs.text:
The worker never ingests the same thing twice, and never destroys an earlier copy.

You add What happens The same link again (tracking junk, case or trailing slash differ) sb add says already known; nothing is queued twice A link that is already a note in the wiki sb add skips it and names the page (already in the wiki as [[...]]) A link already ingested, but never seen by sb add (for example through sb ingest) Queued, then skipped at run time with no model call (skipped); the page is fetched once more first The same PDF or clip dropped in inbox/ again, even renamed Recognised by its bytes, removed from the inbox, reported as a duplicate A different PDF with the same file name Both kept: the new one is stored as name (2).pdf and processed The same text under another path or URL Caught when ingested, by a hash of its text: skipped A page whose content changed since you ingested it Skipped (same URL). To redo it: sb ingest URL --force A link you deleted from the wiki and want again The queue still remembers it as done: sb drop URL, then sb add URL The same email again Recognised by its Message-ID and marked seen, not saved twice

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Pick one route. They install the same program; every command after this page is identical. If you are new, the getting started tutorial uses this page and then goes on to a first note.

Route Command Homebrew (macOS) brew install rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli uv from git uv tool install git+https://github.com/RubenAmaury/esbi-cli A built wheel uv tool install esbi_cli-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl From a source checkout uv tool install --editable . Other systems Not supported

You need Python 3.12 or later, which Homebrew and uv install for you, and git if you want version history (optional). On macOS that means macOS 13 or later: PDFs are read with PDFium, whose prebuilt packages need it. The whole PDF part of the install is about 8 MB, 214 MB less than the PDF stack it replaced, which no longer exists. On macOS 12 or older the install stops with no matching distribution found for pypdfium2: see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Homebrew (macOS)
docs.text:
brew install rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli

This adds the project's tap, installs Python 3.13 and sb. Check it:

sb version

The caveats Homebrew prints at the end tell you the next commands: sb init, sb doctor, sb schedule install, and brew install ollama for local models.

docs.title: uv
docs.text:
uv installs command-line tools into their own environments. If you do not have it:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

Open a new terminal, then:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/RubenAmaury/esbi-cli

It ends with:

Installed 1 executable: sb

sb version

0.1.0

docs.title: A built wheel
docs.text:
Every GitHub release has a wheel attached (esbi_cli-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl; note the underscore). Download it, then:

uv tool install ~/Downloads/esbi_cli-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl

You can build one yourself from a checkout with uv build (the wheel appears in dist/).

docs.title: From a source checkout
docs.text:
For development, or to run the latest code. Changes to the code take effect at once.

git clone https://github.com/RubenAmaury/esbi-cli

Then, inside the folder:

uv tool install --editable .

If you develop with uv sync and the folder lives in an iCloud-synced location such as ~/Documents, see Troubleshooting; CONTRIBUTING covers the development setup.

docs.title: Other systems (not supported)
docs.text:
macOS is the only supported platform for now. Linux and Windows (WSL included) are not supported, and nothing is promised there. sb doctor says so on any other system: WARN platform: esbi-cli is only supported on macOS for now (... it may work, nothing is promised).

For people who try anyway: Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 were tried in containers, and the problems found there were fixed, so it may work. Install with uv tool install esbi-cli (uv fetches its own Python, which matters on 22.04, whose system Python is too old). There is no launchd: the nightly job is a cron line that sb schedule status and sb init --nightly print (Run it every night). Email capture needs a Secret Service for the password (Email where there is no keyring). WSL and native Windows were not tried at all.

docs.title: If sb is not found
docs.text:
sb: command not found means the folder uv puts tools in is not on your PATH. uv printed a warning when it installed; the fix is:

uv tool update-shell

Then open a new terminal. sb doctor prints a WARN global install line with the same cause. Homebrew puts sb in /opt/homebrew/bin, which is on the PATH of a normal Homebrew install.

docs.title: What an installed copy needs
docs.text: Nothing from a source checkout: the starter configuration, the schema, the setup wizards and the Web Clipper templates are inside the package.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
sb init

then sb doctor. The walk-through is Getting started; the way to a model is Choose how the notes are written. To remove it, see Update and uninstall.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: Once a day esbi-cli asks GitHub whether a newer release exists, and a command run in a terminal prints one line when there is one. Nothing installs by itself: sb update shows the command for the way you installed it and asks first. Update esbi-cli explains it, and how to turn the check off ([update] check = false).

docs.title: Manage the queue and old notes
docs.text: Everything you add waits in the queue until sb run works through it. This page is about looking at the queue, getting a failed source through, and rebuilding notes. How sources get in is in Get sources in.

docs.title: See what is queued
docs.text:
sb status

queued: 3
processing: 0
done: 5
failed: 0
State Meaning queued Waiting for a run (also: failed once or twice and will be tried again) processing A run is working on it now done A note was written, or the source was already in the wiki failed Failed three times and is parked until you decide

sb status also lists each parked source with its last error. The names of what is waiting are in today's daily index under Tomorrow's queue (the oldest 20), and sources being retried show there too, under To review, with the attempt number and the error.

sb run scans inbox/ first. To queue what is in inbox/ without running anything, use sb scan.

docs.title: Run a few at a time
docs.text:
sb run --limit 3

A run stops by itself after max_sources_per_run sources (20), max_tokens_per_run tokens (300,000) or, when you set it, max_usd_per_run (an estimated cost in USD), and says so: Stopped early (max_sources); the rest stays queued for the next run. The rest is not lost: after the nightly run, the next hourly tick runs another batch whenever sources are queued, whatever stopped the last one, up to max_batches_per_day scheduled batches a day (6 by default, the nightly one included; see Run it every night).

docs.title: Retry a failed source
docs.text:
A source that fails is tried again on later runs. sb run names it and the reason when it fails (! TITLE: attempt 1 of 3 failed, will be tried again: ...). After the third failure it is parked as failed, and the line says so (attempt 3 of 3 failed, parked):

sb status

queued: 0
processing: 0
done: 2
failed: 1
  failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoesNotExist12345 (ExtractError: Could not fetch https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoesNotExist12345: Client error '404 Not Found' for url 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoesNotExist12345'
For more information check: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/404)

Read the error, fix the cause, then put it back:

sb retry

Requeued 1 source.

sb retry URL requeues only that one; sb retry with nothing parked prints Nothing to retry. The next sb run tries again. If the cause is not yours to fix (a dead link), forget it:

sb drop https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoesNotExist12345

Dropped https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DoesNotExist12345

Common causes and what to do:

Last error What it means Do No readable article content found at ... The page is a login wall, mostly scripts, or very short Clip it with the Web Clipper, or sb drop it Could not fetch ...: Client error '404 Not Found' The link is dead sb drop it Refused to fetch ...: localhost resolves to a non-public address Only public addresses are fetched, by design Save the page as a Markdown file and drop it in inbox/ PDF has almost no extractable text (scanned?) A scan Turn on OCR and sb retry ... has no readable text (a photo or a diagram?) An image with no text in it sb drop it; the worker does not describe pictures A timeout, or a model error The model was too slow for this input Try a stronger model, or raise timeout_seconds; then sb retry

The whole list of messages, by symptom, is in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Stop a run and continue later
docs.text: Press Ctrl-C (or send SIGTERM). What was not finished stays in the queue, and the source that was being read goes back without counting an attempt: it is not a failure. The run says Interrupted: 1 item put back in the queue. and exits with 130 (143 for SIGTERM). A note is never cut in half: if the signal arrives while a note is being written, the run waits until it is whole, then stops. Run sb run again whenever you like; an interrupted scheduled run does not count as that night's run, so the job tries again. sb ingest and sb reingest stop the same way. If the model goes away (The LLM is unreachable (is Ollama running?)), the run stops and nothing is counted against the sources.

docs.title: Forget a source and add it again
docs.text:
The queue remembers a source as done even after you delete its note, so adding the same link says already known. To redo it:

sb drop https://example.com/post

sb add https://example.com/post

If the note is still in the wiki, sb add skips the link and names the note; to rebuild that note instead, see below, or use sb ingest URL --force.

docs.title: Rebuild old notes
docs.text:
sb reingest rebuilds source notes from the originals in raw/ with the current pipeline. Use it after an update that says the note format changed, after you switch to a better model, after you change [notes].language, or when a note came out badly. It needs no network. It keeps your read ticks, dates and tags, and keeps every [[link]] to the note valid.

Rebuild every note that is not yet in the current format (format: 2):

sb reingest

Rebuild only the notes whose title contains a word:

sb reingest "Active recall"

[1/1] Active recall versus rereading
    ... synthesis
    ... connections
Vault tagged pre-reingest-2026-10-03 (undo: git -C ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi reset --hard pre-reingest-2026-10-03)
rebuilt: 1, skipped: 0, failed: 0

Rebuild everything again, even notes already in the current format:

sb reingest --all

With nothing to rebuild it prints rebuilt: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 0 and touches nothing.

Things to know:

  • Language. Notes are written in the language the config names when they are rebuilt. Changing [notes].language never rewrites old notes by itself; sb reingest --all rebuilds every note in the new language (concept pages keep a ## Desde or ## From section per source, and the rebuilt note's sections are swapped for ones in the new language; sections of notes you do not rebuild stay as they were). New notes follow the setting at once.
  • Undo. Before it touches anything it commits the vault and tags it pre-reingest-<date>. To go back: git -C ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi reset --hard pre-reingest-2026-10-03 (use your vault path and the tag it printed).
  • It replaces the note. Edits you made in the body of a source note are not kept (the note is written again from the original); the git tag has the old version. Tags you added and the read state are kept.
  • Resumable. If it stops (the model went away, the Mac slept, Ctrl-C), run sb reingest again: notes already rebuilt carry format: 2 and are skipped. A full rebuild of 24 notes took about 2.5 hours on an 8 GB Mac.
  • Needs git. It refuses without a git history, because the undo depends on it.
  • One at a time. It takes the run lock, so it will not start while sb run works: Another run is in progress; try again when it finishes.
  • A note whose original is missing from raw/ is skipped and listed with the reason.

docs.title: Choose how the notes are written
docs.text:
The notes are written by a language model. You choose where it runs, per task, in config.toml (sb init writes a first version). All the kinds below work with the same commands, and you can change your mind at any time (Switch models).

Kind model = What leaves your machine Good for Local, Ollama ollama/llama3.2:latest Nothing Privacy, no cost; a small model writes useful but plain notes Local, LM Studio lmstudio/<identifier> (see lms ls) Nothing Same, with LM Studio's model library; set base_url if the server is not on port 1234 Your Claude subscription claude-cli/default Source text goes to Anthropic through the official claude tool Noticeably better notes with no per-token bill; counts against your plan's usage windows Your ChatGPT plan codex-cli/default Source text goes to OpenAI through the official codex tool; email never does Better notes with no per-token bill; about 8,500 tokens of overhead per call, so best for the writing model of the nightly run An API key anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5, openai/gpt-... (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with base_url) Source text goes to that provider Better notes, billed per token

Which one? Start with Ollama and llama3.2: it is free, private and runs on an 8 GB Mac. If the notes are too thin, move only the writing model ([llm.synthesize]) to your subscription or an API and keep the reading local. Different models for different jobs shows how.

docs.title: Install Ollama and a model
docs.text:
Ollama runs models on your machine. On a Mac:

brew install ollama

brew services start ollama

Without Homebrew, use the installer on ollama.com/download. Check that it answers:

curl http://localhost:11434

Ollama is running

Download a model once, then list what you have:

ollama pull llama3.2

ollama list

What is known to work, on an 8 GB Apple Silicon Mac:

Model Size Use it for llama3.2 (3B) 2.0 GB The default: reading and writing notes qwen3:4b 2.5 GB sb ask: it cites the right page more often, but is about ten times slower. As the writing model it timed out at 900 s on 8 GB qwen3:8b 5.2 GB Tight on 8 GB; comfortable on 16 GB qwen3-vl:2b-instruct 1.9 GB Only for images and scanned PDFs nomic-embed-text 274 MB Only for search by meaning

Models whose name ends in -cloud run on Ollama's servers, not on your machine; the worker treats them as sending text out.

docs.title: Use LM Studio
docs.text:
Install LM Studio, download a model, load it, and start the local server (Developer tab). Find the identifier LM Studio uses for the model:

lms ls

Then tell sb init (or edit the config):

sb init --model local --runtime lmstudio --local-model qwen2.5-7b-instruct

In the config it looks like model = "lmstudio/qwen2.5-7b-instruct". sb doctor checks that LM Studio answers and serves that identifier.

docs.title: Use an Ollama server on another machine
docs.text:
Point the model at it with base_url:

[llm.summarize]
model = "ollama/qwen3:8b"
base_url = "http://192.168.1.50:11434"

Be clear about what this means: the text of your notes goes to that machine. The worker treats it like a cloud model: email is kept off it, a remote [llm.private] is refused, and sb doctor shows WARN server summarize for as long as it is set.

docs.title: Use an API key
docs.text:
Set the key in your environment, then choose an anthropic/... or openai/... model:

[llm.summarize]
model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

The key is never written in config.toml. If it lives in a variable with another name, add api_key_env = "MY_VARIABLE". For a service that speaks the OpenAI protocol (OpenRouter, a company gateway) use openai/<model> with a base_url. A nightly job started by launchd does not see variables from your shell profile, so for unattended runs a local model or the subscription is simpler. Full settings: Configuration.

docs.title: Use your Claude subscription
docs.text:
Install Claude Code, then log in once:

claude auth login

Then set model = "claude-cli/default" for a task (sb init --model subscription writes it for all of them). sb doctor checks the login. The app starts claude with its tools, settings and plugins switched off, because otherwise every call would carry hundreds of thousands of tokens of your own setup.

docs.title: Use your ChatGPT plan
docs.text:
Install OpenAI's codex tool, then log in once:

codex login

Then set model = "codex-cli/default" (the model your Codex is set to) or codex-cli/<model> for a task. sb doctor checks that codex is installed and that codex login status says you are logged in. The call runs read-only in an empty scratch folder with the tool's own tools and your Codex settings switched off. A fallback works as it does for the other providers: a spent usage window or a lost login stops the call, and the fallback takes over.

What was measured, once, against codex-cli 0.146.0 on a ChatGPT plan: the strict schema the worker sends was accepted, a call takes 9 to 12 seconds, and each call carries about 8,500 tokens of the tool's own prompt on top of yours. That overhead is why it suits the model that makes a few calls per source ([llm.synthesize]) and not the one that reads every chunk ([llm.summarize], many calls: keep it local). Like any model that sends text out, it is never shown email: keep a local [llm.private].

[llm.synthesize]
model = "codex-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

docs.title: Email always stays local
docs.text:
If any model is a cloud kind (an API, claude-cli, codex-cli, a remote server), add a local [llm.private] model: emails are written only by it, and cloud models are never shown email pages. Without it, emails are refused while a cloud model is set (sb doctor warns).

[llm.summarize]
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"   # used when the main model cannot be reached

[llm.private]
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

docs.title: Different models for different jobs
docs.text:
[llm.summarize] reads each chunk of a long source (many small calls), [llm.synthesize] writes the digest and the connections (a few calls), [llm.ask] answers questions, and [llm.private] reads email. synthesize and ask fall back to [llm.summarize] when absent; private, ocr and embed are simply off. Example:

[llm.summarize]                # reads each chunk: many cheap calls
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
max_tokens = 1200

[llm.synthesize]               # writes the note: a few calls
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

The full list of settings is in the configuration reference.

docs.title: What a 3B model is good for
docs.text: llama3.2 (3B) reads and writes useful notes and is the right default. Two things it does not do well, measured on real notes: its concept summaries (the ## Summary that sb consolidate writes on a page with several sources) read well but sometimes state a relation between the sources that none of them says, and its diagram relations rarely tie an end to a concept of the note, so the concept map is often left out. The worker checks both and drops what it can prove wrong, but a plausible invention gets through. That is why [run].max_consolidations_per_run is 0 (off) by default: read some summaries from sb consolidate first, and turn the automatic pass on only with a stronger [llm.synthesize] model. See Consolidated summaries.

docs.title: Switch models
docs.text:
Edit config.toml, then check the setup:

sb doctor

sb doctor tells you if the new model is missing (ollama pull ...), unreachable or has no key. Notes you already have are not changed by a new model; only new sources use it. To rewrite the old notes with it, run sb reingest.

If you have changed nightly_time, run sb schedule install again. Nothing else needs reinstalling.

docs.title: Compare models on your own notes
docs.text:
sb bench runs the same ingest and question cases, built from your own vault, through each model, and prints a table: success rate, share needing no retry, median latency, tokens, estimated cost, the share written in the right language ([notes].language), and whether answers cite the right page. It never writes to the wiki and never changes your config.

sb bench --models ollama/llama3.2:latest,ollama/qwen3:4b --cases 3

It needs a vault with some sources and concepts in it already. It ends with a suggestion for each task (a model is only suggested when it succeeds on at least 80% of cases) and saves the report in .esbi/bench/. To price a cloud model, give it a rate in [bench.prices]; see Configuration. To measure how well sb ask finds the right pages, use sb eval.

docs.title: Choosing the OCR model
docs.text:
[llm.ocr] reads images and scanned PDFs (see Images and scanned PDFs). It is optional, and a choice you make and can see: sb init asks (default No), sb ocr status shows whether it is on, the model, whether Ollama has it, its size and your machine's memory, sb ocr enable [--model NAME] [--pull] turns it on and sb ocr disable turns it off while keeping the model. It must be a vision model served by Ollama on your machine; the recommended one is qwen3-vl:2b-instruct (1.9 GB download, 3.4 GB in memory at an 8K context, which leaves room for the text model because Ollama keeps one at a time). Use the -instruct tag: the plain qwen3-vl:2b tag is the "thinking" variant.

deepseek-ocr:3b (6.7 GB, needs Ollama 0.13.0 or later) is a known choice for a machine with 16 GB of memory or more, and it is asked with the fixed instruction it needs (a general one does not work for it); it is never the default. It was measured unusable on an 8 GB Mac: it loads at about 10 GB and took 7 to 8 minutes to read a small image that qwen3-vl:2b-instruct reads in seconds (roughly 100 times slower). It was not measured above 8 GB. sb ocr status and sb doctor warn (ocr memory) when your machine has less memory than the model you chose wants. Any other Ollama vision model also works and gets a general instruction; the worker only knows the two above.

Measured on an 8 GB Apple M2 with Ollama 0.13.5, while other programs were also using the model server (so the times are pessimistic). Similarity is the character-level ratio against the known text (1.0 is perfect). The inputs: a real paper page rasterised at 130 dpi (English, 4,500 characters), a rendered Spanish page, a dark-theme code screenshot, a photo of a Spanish slide (rotated, blurred, noisy, JPEG), a Spanish diagram with five labels, and a picture with no text.

Engine English page Spanish page Code screenshot Slide photo Diagram labels Picture with no text Time per page qwen3-vl:2b-instruct (chosen) 0.996 1.000 1.000 0.982 1.000 answers [img] 2 to 29 s granite3.2-vision (2.4 GB) 0.537 0.717 0.675 0.982 1.000 invents 725 characters 12 to 63 s qwen2.5vl:3b (3.2 GB) does not load: its vision step asks Metal for 6.6 GiB and this Mac allows 5.7 GiB macOS Vision (for reference) 0.999 1.000 0.973 0.982 0.805 nothing 0.2 to 2.6 s

A scanned PDF (two pages of the same paper) scored 0.996 with qwen3-vl:2b-instruct, 24 s per page. The 0.982 on the slide is the model writing - for the bullet •; the words are all right.

Why this one: it is the only candidate that is both accurate and honest about an empty picture (granite writes text that is not there), it runs on Ollama, and it fits next to the text model. macOS Vision is faster and as accurate, but only exists on macOS and would need a bridge library; it is a possible later addition behind the same [llm.ocr] seam. Not tried: glm-ocr, qwen3.5 and minicpm-v4.6 need a newer Ollama than 0.13.5 (the pull is refused), deepseek-ocr is 6.7 GB (see above for what it did on 8 GB), and Tesseract needs a system install. If you upgrade Ollama, glm-ocr (2.2 GB, built for documents) is worth measuring against these numbers.

What these tests do not show: all inputs are clean renderings or one synthetic "photo", not a pile of real phone photos; handwriting, tables, multi-column layouts and very small print were not measured. Treat the numbers as a floor for clean text and a guess for everything else.

docs.title: Move to a new Mac
docs.text: Moving takes four things: the program, a model, your vault, and your settings. The vault and the config are plain files, so this is a copy and a check. Work through it in order.

docs.title: 1. Stop the nightly job
docs.text:
So two Macs do not work on one vault at once:

sb schedule uninstall

docs.title: 2. Make sure the vault is current
docs.text: Run sb index: it commits, and pushes if you have a remote.

docs.title: 3. Copy these
docs.text:
To a drive, a cloud folder or the git remote:

What Where The whole vault folder The vault path in your config, for example ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi The config file ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml (sb info prints its path) Your golden questions, if any <vault>/.esbi/golden.jsonl: inside the vault folder, so it comes with it if you copy the folder

With a git remote the notes, SCHEMA.md and your golden questions travel through it, but your other own files (inbox/, .obsidian/) do not: copy the whole folder, or read Back up and restore.

docs.title: 4. Email only
docs.text: Note the Gmail address. You will store the app password again; it stays in the Keychain and is not copied.

docs.title: 1. Install the program
docs.text: See Install.

docs.title: 2. Get a model
docs.text: For a local model, install Ollama and pull the same models (ollama list on the old Mac shows which): Install Ollama and a model. For your subscription: claude auth login.

docs.title: 3. Copy the vault and the config
docs.text: Put the vault in the same place (or any place) and the config at ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml. If the vault's path is different, edit vault in the config.

docs.title: 4. Check everything
docs.text:
sb doctor

Fix what it says: a model to pull, a login, the Obsidian vault to open (Open folder as vault).

docs.title: 5. Email only
docs.text:
sb email set-password

Then sb email fetch to test.

docs.title: 6. Install the nightly job
docs.text:
sb schedule install

Allow Documents access when macOS asks (Run it every night).

docs.title: 7. Web Clipper only
docs.text: Install the extension again and import the templates with sb setup clipper: they are not stored in the vault.

docs.title: What does not move
docs.text:
• The queue. It lives in <vault>/.esbi/ and comes along if you copy the folder. If you moved through git it is gone: sources not yet processed need adding again.
  • The Keychain password. Store it again.
  • Ollama's models. Pull them again.
  • launchd's job. Install it again on the new Mac.

Do not run the nightly job on both Macs against a vault in a synced folder at the same time: the run lock is a file lock on one machine, so it cannot protect two.

docs.title: Run it every night
docs.text:
A nightly job runs sb run for you at a time you choose, so the queue is worked through while you sleep and the morning index is waiting. It is optional: sb run by hand does the same.

The job runs sb run --if-due. --if-due does real work only when a scheduled batch is due. The first batch of the day is due after nightly_time (default 03:00, set under [run]); once it has run, a check with nothing to do prints Not due: the nightly run already happened. and stops, which is why it is safe to ask for it every hour. A run stopped by a model outage, or interrupted (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, a shutdown), does not count as the nightly run, so the next check retries it; manual sb runs never count.

The hourly tick drains the queue. A run stops at [run].max_sources_per_run sources (20 by default), at max_tokens_per_run tokens or, when you set it, at max_usd_per_run. Once the nightly run has happened, whenever sources are queued the next hourly tick is due again and runs the next batch, one batch per tick, whatever ended the last batch: one of those limits, or an empty queue that filled again later (links you sb add during the day). The check counts what is queued and the files waiting in inbox/ that a run can read (an image without an OCR model does not count). New mail is fetched by the nightly run, so on its own it waits for the next night. Before 0.4.0 only a batch that stopped at the source limit was continued, so a batch that stopped on its token budget (common with long PDFs) waited for the next night. At most [run].max_batches_per_day scheduled batches run a day (a whole number of at least 1, default 6), counted from nightly_time and including the nightly run itself; this cap is what bounds a day's work and spend, so a large backlog cannot keep the model busy all day: with the defaults, up to 6 batches of 20 sources, then the rest waits for the next night. A run stopped by an outage or an interruption does not count towards it, and neither does a manual sb run. The hourly tick never continues after a scheduled run that stopped for an outage or an interruption: that waits for the next night (when it was the nightly run itself, the next check retries it, as above), and it never starts while another run is active. To cap what a day can cost, set max_usd_per_run (see [run]): the scheduled batches of a day then cost about max_batches_per_day times it at most (the check happens between sources, so the source being read finishes first).

The job is supported on macOS (launchd). On other systems, which are not supported, you can try cron.

docs.title: macOS (launchd)
docs.text:
Install it once:

sb schedule install

Installed ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.esbi-cli.nightly.plist
Runs every day at 03:00 (or at the next wake). Log: ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/.esbi/logs/nightly.log

(Or answer yes to the nightly question in sb init, or run sb init --nightly 03:00 on a new config.) Check it:

sb schedule status

installed: yes
loaded: yes

What it installs is a launchd agent that runs sb run --if-due at the time you set, at login, and every hour as a safety net. If the Mac is asleep at the set time, launchd starts the job at the next wake (unlike cron, which skips it). The run is wrapped in caffeinate -i, so the Mac cannot idle-sleep in the middle of it. The hourly timer alone would not be enough, because launchd drops interval ticks that fall while the Mac sleeps.

docs.title: First run: macOS asks for permission
docs.text:
The job reads ~/Documents (your vault, the config). macOS's privacy protection shows a dialog the first time, like "Python would like to access files in your Documents folder". Click Allow. Until you do, the job waits silently and looks "running" forever. If you missed the dialog: System Settings, Privacy & Security, Files & Folders (or Full Disk Access), enable the Python framework (/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/.../Python.app), then restart the job:

launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.esbi-cli.nightly

An agent or script cannot click that dialog for you.

docs.title: Choose the time
docs.text:
Set nightly_time = "HH:MM" (24 hours) under [run] in config.toml, then install again so launchd is set for the new time:

sb schedule install

The due check follows the config at once, but launchd only fires at the time it was installed for. sb doctor warns when the two differ:

  WARN nightly job: installed for 03:00 but config.toml says 04:30
         fix: sb schedule install

docs.title: Wake the Mac for it
docs.text:
The Mac only works while awake. To have it awake for the run, wake it at the same time or a minute later. For 04:30:

sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 04:30:00

It needs sudo, so it is yours to run. Never wake it earlier than nightly_time: a run is only due from that moment, so an earlier wake finds nothing to do and the Mac goes back to sleep. Check it with pmset -g sched. Ollama must also be running (the Homebrew service starts it at login).

docs.title: Check that it works
docs.text:
sb doctor

  ok   last run: 2026-10-03 03:00: 2 ingested, 0 failed
  ok   nightly job: installed and loaded, runs at 03:00
  • WARN last run: no scheduled run yet: the job has not run since you installed it.
  • WARN last run: 2026-10-03 03:00: the model server was unreachable (nothing was lost; the sources stay queued): the latest run stopped because the model could not be reached. Start Ollama (brew services start ollama) or check the model line, then run sb run; the hourly check retries by itself too. The next run that reaches the model clears the warning.
  • The log is <vault>/.esbi/logs/nightly.log; it is trimmed by itself. A healthy hourly check with nothing queued (or with the day's batches used up) ends in Not due: the nightly run already happened.
  • Every run, manual or scheduled, is listed under Ejecuciones in the daily note.
  • launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.esbi-cli.nightly | grep -E "state|last exit" shows launchd's own view.

docs.title: Remove it
docs.text:
sb schedule uninstall

Removed.

docs.title: After you update or move sb
docs.text: The job remembers where sb lives and which config it uses. After updating, reinstalling or moving sb, or moving the config, run sb schedule install again.

docs.title: Other systems: cron (not supported)
docs.text:
macOS is the only supported platform for now; this section is for people who try another system anyway, and nothing here is promised. There is no launchd there, so use cron (or any scheduler that can run a command every hour). sb init --nightly 03:00 prints the line to use, and so do sb schedule install, status and uninstall. install and uninstall stop with exit code 1 and error: the nightly job uses launchd, which only macOS has, because they cannot do what was asked; status has nothing to query, so it prints the line and exits 0:

Nightly job: this system has no launchd. Add this to cron (every hour: the first tick after [run].nightly_time runs the nightly batch, later ones drain what is queued, up to [run].max_batches_per_day batches a day):
  0 * * * * /home/you/.local/bin/sb run --if-due --config /home/you/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml

The line names sb by its absolute path, quotes a path that has spaces and writes a % as \% (in a crontab a bare % means a new line). Copy it as printed.

Add it with:

crontab -e

Two details that cron needs and a terminal does not:

  1. sb must be named by its full path. cron's PATH is only /usr/bin:/bin, which has no ~/.local/bin, where uv tool and pipx put sb; a bare sb is "not found" every hour and the nightly job never runs, with nothing to tell you. The printed line already has the path. An older version printed a bare sb: if you copied that line, replace sb with the output of command -v sb.
  2. Give it what the model needs. For Ollama running as a service there is nothing to add. For your subscription, claude must be on cron's PATH; for an API key, the key must be set in the crontab (a variable line above the job), which stores it in plain text.

A full line, with a log:

0 * * * * /home/you/.local/bin/sb run --if-due --config /home/you/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml >> /home/you/esbi-cli.log 2>&1

Hourly is intentional: --if-due means only the first check after nightly_time does the first batch (and, while sources are queued, one more batch per hourly check, up to max_batches_per_day), and if the machine was off at 03:00 the first check after it comes back does it. nightly_time still decides when a run counts as due. It was tried on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 in containers; launchd on macOS is the only supported way (see Other systems).

WSL and native Windows were not tried (WSL does not run cron unless systemd is enabled, to name one thing); they are not supported.

docs.title: Does the job need my machine to be on?
docs.text: Yes: it runs on your machine, with your models. With a subscription or an API the model is elsewhere, but the worker still runs here. See Use it offline for what works without a network.

docs.title: Read your notes and tick what you have read
docs.text: The daily index is where the day starts. This page is the routine: open it, read, tick, register. The meaning of every section is in The daily index; how a note is laid out is in How a note is made.

docs.title: Open today's index
docs.text:
sb today
  • With viewer = "obsidian" it opens today's note in Obsidian through an obsidian:// link. Obsidian must know the vault: open the folder once with Open folder as vault.
  • With viewer = "none" it prints the path of the file, to open in any Markdown editor:
~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

If today's note does not exist yet it is built first. In Obsidian you can also start from Home.md, which links to it.

docs.title: Read a note
docs.text: Under Processed today each new source is a checkbox with a one-line summary. Open a source from there. Read the executive summary first and decide whether the source deserves your time; the detailed summary, key ideas, glossary, quotes and connections follow. A note is a draft written by a model, so trust what it quotes (quotes are checked against the source) and treat connections and the diagram as hints: see Trust: what can be wrong.

docs.title: Tick what you have read
docs.text:
Change the box of a source to - [x] in the daily note, save, and run:

sb index

Marked 1 source as read.
Wrote wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

The source's status becomes read, its read date is set to today, and it shows under Read from then on. Ticks in earlier days' notes count too, so a tick you forgot to register is not lost. Unticking undoes it: untick the box in the note of the day the source was processed, run sb index (or sb run), and the source goes back to processed (Put 1 source back to unread.) and leaves Read. Only that day's note counts for this; a source with no box there is left as it is.

You do not have to run sb index: every sb run registers your ticks before it rebuilds the note. The tick is only read from a line shaped - [x] [[Source title]].

docs.title: Edit a note
docs.text:
The notes are yours. You can fix a sentence, add tags, add your own thoughts, or add links. The worker will not overwrite an edit on its own. Two exceptions: sb reingest writes a source note again from its original (its git tag keeps your version), and each new source that mentions a concept adds a ## From [[source]] section to that concept's page (your own text on the page stays).

Do not edit anything between <!-- esbi:start --> and <!-- esbi:end --> in Home.md: the worker rewrites that block. The rest of Home.md is yours.

docs.title: Find a note again
docs.text:
• In Obsidian: search, the graph, and backlinks work as usual.
  • From the command line: sb ask "..." (Ask your wiki).
  • index.md in the vault is a catalogue of every page, rebuilt by the worker.

docs.title: If a note looks wrong
docs.text: Edit it, or rebuild it: sb reingest "<part of its title>". A note that is in English or thin usually means the model is too small: see Choose how the notes are written.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Find your symptom, read the message exactly as it appears, and follow the fix. Start with the command that checks everything:

sb doctor

Each line says ok, WARN or FAIL, and what to do under anything that is not fine. Most problems on this page show up there first. If yours is not here, open an issue and paste the output of sb doctor (it contains no secrets).

On this page: install and start, the model, sources, asking, the nightly job, mail, git and backup, files, disks and unusual setups.

docs.title: sb is not found
docs.text:
sb: command not found

The folder that holds sb is not on your PATH. With uv, run uv tool update-shell and open a new terminal. sb doctor shows WARN global install: sb is not on your PATH for the same reason. See Install.

docs.title: The package cannot be imported (macOS hidden files)
docs.text:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'esbi_cli'

This only happens when you run from a source checkout with uv sync, and the environment lives in ~/Documents, where iCloud keeps marking .venv files hidden (Python 3.13 then skips them). Keep the environment outside it, for good:

export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$HOME/.local/share/venvs/esbi-cli"

then uv sync again. The quick fix is chflags -R nohidden .venv. A normal install with Homebrew or uv tool install is not affected.

docs.title: No config file is found
docs.text:
error: No config.toml found (looked in: ...)

sb doctor shows FAIL config. You have not run sb init, or the config is somewhere else. Run sb init, or point at the file with --config PATH or the ESBI_CONFIG variable. sb info prints the file in use. A config.toml in the current folder is never read, on purpose. If you pass --config (or set ESBI_CONFIG) with a path that does not exist, the command stops with error: config file not found: PATH; only the default places are tried one after the other.

docs.title: The config has a mistake
docs.text: Message Fix error: config.toml needs [paths].vault Add vault = "..." under [paths] error: [run].nightly_time must look like HH:MM (24 hours), got '25:00' Write the time as "03:00" error: [notes].language must be one of: en, es, got 'fr' Use a language the program has; to add one, see Add a language error: [notes].viewer must be "obsidian" or "none", got ... Use one of the two error: Expected ']' at the end of a table declaration (at line 2, column 7) A TOML syntax error: the line and column are in the message error: [llm.summarize] has an unknown key 'num_ctxx' (did you mean 'num_ctx'?). Valid keys: ... A key is misspelled. The message names the section, the key and the valid keys. The same check covers every section error: [run].max_chunks must be a whole number, got 'ten' A value has the wrong type (text where a number goes, "true" where true goes). Fix the value as the message says error: config file not found: PATH The file given with --config (or ESBI_CONFIG) does not exist. Check the path

docs.title: The vault is not found
docs.text:
error: vault not found: ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi (run `sb init`, or fix [paths].vault)

[paths].vault points at a folder that does not exist: a typo, an unmounted drive, a cloud folder not synced yet. Every command that opens the vault stops here and creates nothing (before, it made the folder and a .esbi/ inside it, so a mistyped path became a second, empty vault). With --json the error object has the code vault_not_found. Fix the path, or run sb init --vault PATH. sb doctor, sb init and the commands that only edit the config (sb ocr ..., sb email set-password) still work without it, so sb doctor is the way to see what is wrong.

docs.title: The vault is not recognised
docs.text:
FAIL vault: ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi is not a esbi-cli vault (SCHEMA.md or wiki/ missing)
         fix: fix [paths].vault in config.toml

vault points at a folder that sb init did not make. Fix the path, or run sb init --vault PATH to create what is missing. After a restore from git the same message appears until you run sb init (Back up and restore).

docs.title: No matching distribution for pypdfium2
docs.text:
No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ... pypdfium2 ... no matching distribution found ...

esbi-cli reads PDFs with pypdfium2, and its prebuilt packages exist only for macOS 13 or later (and Linux, which is not a supported system). On macOS 12 or older the installer finds no package for your system and stops. Update macOS (there is no other PDF engine to fall back to), or install esbi-cli on a machine that runs macOS 13 or later.

docs.title: The shell says no matches found
docs.text:
zsh: no matches found: https://example.com/post?id=7

A link with ? or & must be in quotes: sb add "https://example.com/post?id=7".

docs.title: The model is not reachable
docs.text:
The LLM is unreachable (is Ollama running?). Nothing was lost; sources stay queued.

  FAIL model summarize: Ollama is not reachable at http://localhost:11434
         fix: brew services start ollama (or open the Ollama app)

Ollama is not running, or base_url is wrong. Start it (brew services start ollama, or open the app) and check curl http://localhost:11434 answers Ollama is running. The run stopped and nothing was counted against your sources: run sb run again. The daily index is still rebuilt after a failed run, and it tells you in the morning: the first line under To review says the model server was unreachable in the last run and how many sources are waiting, and sb doctor shows WARN last run with the same fix. Both go away after a run that reaches the model.

docs.title: The model is not installed
docs.text:
FAIL model summarize: ollama/llama3.2:latest is not installed
         fix: ollama pull llama3.2:latest

Download it: ollama pull llama3.2. ollama list shows what you have.

docs.title: LM Studio does not answer
docs.text:
FAIL model summarize: LM Studio is not reachable at http://localhost:1234/v1
         fix: open LM Studio, load a model, and start the local server (Developer tab)

  FAIL model summarize: LM Studio does not serve 'x'
         fix: use one of: qwen2.5-7b-instruct

Start the server, and use the identifier lms ls shows in model = "lmstudio/...".

docs.title: The subscription does not work
docs.text: Message Fix FAIL model ...: the claude command is not installed Install Claude Code FAIL model ...: claude is not logged in claude auth login claude: ... Run claude auth login. (during a run) Your login expired: claude auth login claude: ... with a usage-limit message You spent a usage window of your plan. The run stopped like any model outage, nothing is lost, and the next run resumes. Set a local fallback to keep going meanwhile claude gave no answer within 300s A timeout for one source; raise timeout_seconds in that [llm.*] section claude returned no JSON (exit 1): ... The claude tool failed to start; run claude by hand to see why

docs.title: The ChatGPT plan does not work
docs.text: Message Fix FAIL model ...: the codex command is not installed Install OpenAI's codex tool FAIL model ...: codex is not logged in codex login codex (exit 1): ... Run codex login. (during a run) Your login expired: codex login codex (exit 1): ... with a usage-limit message You spent a usage window of your plan. The run stopped like any model outage, nothing is lost, and the next run resumes. A local fallback keeps it going meanwhile codex gave no answer within 300s A timeout for one source; raise timeout_seconds in that [llm.*] section. Each call also carries about 8,500 tokens of the tool's own overhead, so it is slower than it looks codex (exit 1): Unknown feature flag ... Your Codex is a different version from the one the worker was checked against (0.146.0) and no longer knows a feature the worker switches off. Update esbi-cli; or open an issue with the message

docs.title: An API key is missing
docs.text:
FAIL model summarize: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set
         fix: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...

During a run the message is Environment variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set. Set the variable in your shell profile and open a new terminal. A nightly job started by launchd does not read your profile, so for unattended runs prefer a local model or the subscription. A rejected key shows HTTP 401 in the message.

docs.title: The model name is not understood
docs.text:
FAIL model summarize: unknown provider in 'foo/bar'
         fix: use ollama/, lmstudio/, openai/, anthropic/, claude-cli/ or codex-cli/

Other forms: Model must look like '<provider>/<name>', and Unknown LLM provider 'x'; use one of [...]. Write the model as provider/name.

docs.title: There is no summarize section
docs.text:
No [llm.summarize] section in config

[llm.summarize] is required. Add it (Configuration), or run sb init for a fresh config.

docs.title: The model is too slow, or times out
docs.text: A line like .../api/chat gave no answer within 300s means one chunk or source took longer than timeout_seconds. It fails that source, not the run. Options: raise timeout_seconds; set max_tokens on the model that reads chunks (small models sometimes loop, and the cap turns a 5-minute timeout into seconds); use a smaller max_source_chars; or a faster model. Expect 3 to 15 minutes per source with a small local model.

docs.title: Notes come out in the wrong language or thin
docs.text: The model is too small. The worker already retries once when the note comes out in the wrong language, and says The model answered in the wrong language (wanted English) when the second try fails too. Try a larger model for [llm.synthesize] (Choose how the notes are written) and compare with sb bench. Rebuild old notes with sb reingest.

docs.title: A source keeps failing
docs.text:
sb run prints one ! line per failed source with the attempt and the reason; sb status shows each parked source and its last error. A source is tried three times (it is queued while it is being retried), then parked as failed and listed under To review in the daily note. Fix the cause, then sb retry; or sb drop it. Stopping a run yourself is not a failed attempt: after Ctrl-C or SIGTERM the source that was being read goes back to the queue with no attempt counted, so interrupting as often as you like never parks a good source (older versions counted it, and three interruptions parked one).

Last error What it means and what to do No readable article content found at URL The page is a login wall, mostly scripts, or very short. Clip it with the Web Clipper Could not fetch URL: Client error '404 Not Found' ... A dead link: sb drop it Could not fetch URL: ... (a connection error) No network, or the site is down. sb retry later Could not fetch URL: Cannot resolve HOST: ... The name does not exist, or DNS failed Refused to fetch URL: localhost resolves to a non-public address (127.0.0.1) By design, only public addresses are fetched. Save the page as a Markdown file and drop it in inbox/ Refused to fetch URL: Only http(s) URLs are fetched, not 'ftp' Only http and https Refused to fetch URL: The response is larger than 20 MB or ...: The download took more than 120 s Downloads are capped; download the file yourself and add it by path Refused to fetch URL: Too many redirects (more than N) The link loops PDF has almost no extractable text (scanned?): add an [llm.ocr] model ... A scan: turn on OCR PDF has no readable text, even with OCR The OCR model found nothing on any page NAME has no readable text (a photo or a diagram?) An image with fewer than 40 characters of text. The worker does not describe pictures. sb drop it The OCR model could not read NAME: ... The vision model failed: check sb doctor (model ocr) Could not open PDF: ... / Could not open NAME as an image: ... The file is damaged, not what its extension says, or a PDF that needs a password (Could not open PDF: Failed to load document (PDFium: Incorrect password error).). Remove the password (open it in a PDF viewer and export a copy) and add that A PDF note has long runs of short label-like lines, or too few or too many headings A chart-heavy PDF (a slide deck, a report full of plots): the labels of a chart are text in the PDF. The reader drops a short line that the file repeats 8 times or more, short lines packed into one spot of a page and long runs of label-like lines, and keeps at most 8 headings per page (at least 40 per file), the numbered and the biggest first, so a few chart labels can still come out as lines or as headings. The note is still made; a larger model copes better, and the text inside images and charts is not read at all. See How a note is made NAME has almost no text (N chars) A clip with under 40 characters of text after the page chrome of a GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Reddit or YouTube clip was removed. A clip of a login wall, a cookie page or an empty feed is exactly this: nothing but chrome. Open the page again logged in and re-clip it; sb drop the empty one Unsupported file type: .docx Only .pdf, .md and images (with OCR) are read; convert it the run died while reading this The process was killed while reading this source three times in a row (a huge PDF running out of memory). Try a smaller file. A run you stopped with Ctrl-C does not count: see above

docs.title: Warnings after a note is written
docs.text:
These are not errors: the note was written, and the line says what was left out. They appear after the + Title line of sb run (and as warning: for sb ingest).

Warning Meaning Dropped 2 diagram edges: an end was not in the source or the note. The model drew a relation whose end is neither in the source text nor a concept, entity, term or alias of the note, so the worker removed it. Often the concept map is then left out (fewer than two relations remain). Nothing to do; a stronger model invents fewer Only half of chunk 2 of 5 could be read. A chunk of a long source was invalid twice, was read again in two halves, and only one half worked. The note covers the rest of the source and a little less of that chunk. sb reingest TITLE tries again Removed N lines of page chrome from the clip. A clip of GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Reddit or YouTube had menus, sidebars, sign-in or cookie lines; they were removed before reading and counted as stripped_lines in the note. The clip in raw/inbox/ is as it came. Nothing to do; if real text was lost, the original is there Not read: 12 of 52 parts of the source (the last 23% of the text, starting at "...") because the limit of 60 model calls per source ([run].max_calls_per_source) was reached. A very long source (a book) needed more model calls than [run].max_calls_per_source allows, so the reading stopped and the rest is not in the note. The note starts with the same warning (> [!warning] Not read: ..., No leído: ... in Spanish), so you can see it when you read it. Raise the cap in [run] (a source of 40 chunks takes about 55 calls) and rebuild the note with sb reingest; it costs more tokens and time Section 2 was merged without the model (...) In a long source, the model could not merge the notes of a group of chunks (invalid twice, too slow, or no calls left), so code merged the points of that section instead. Nothing was invented; the section is just less condensed Removed 2 link or image address(es) the model wrote that the source does not contain. The model wrote web addresses (links or images) that are not in the source, so the worker removed them and kept the link text. Often a small model inventing a reference; sometimes a hostile page asking for it. Nothing to do. See Prompt injection Could not read chunk 2 of 5; skipped (...) Both halves failed too (or the model timed out): that part of the source is not in the note. Try a larger model for [llm.summarize]

docs.title: Another run is in progress
docs.text:
Another run is in progress; skipping.

Another sb run (or the nightly job, or sb reingest) holds the lock. It ends by itself, and the lock is released even after a crash. sb run exits 0 here; sb reingest says Another run is in progress; try again when it finishes. and exits 1.

docs.title: Files in inbox are not read
docs.text:
Not read, esbi-cli cannot read these files in inbox/: letter.docx, slide.png
  Images: add an [llm.ocr] model to config.toml to read images and scanned PDFs (`sb init --ocr`, docs/reference/configuration.md)

Those files stay in inbox/ and are listed on every scan. Images need OCR; HEIC, Word and other types are not supported: convert them to JPG, PDF or Markdown.

docs.title: A source says it is already in the wiki
docs.text:
Already in the vault as [[Zettelkasten]] (use --force to redo).

Not an error: the same URL or the same text is already a note. See If a source already exists. sb add says Skipped URL: already in the wiki as [[...]].

docs.title: Reading images is slow, or DeepSeek-OCR never finishes
docs.text:
sb ocr status (and sb doctor, WARN ocr memory) says when the model you chose wants more memory than this machine has. deepseek-ocr:3b is a model for 16 GB of memory or more: on an 8 GB Mac it loads at about 10 GB, takes minutes for one small image, and was measured about 100 times slower than the recommended one. Switch with:

sb ocr enable --model qwen3-vl:2b-instruct --pull

A WARN ocr ollama line means Ollama is older than the model needs: brew upgrade ollama, or update the app. See Choosing the OCR model.

docs.title: An email is refused
docs.text:
an email cannot be written by a model that sends text away: add a local model as [llm.private] in config.toml

You have a cloud model and no local [llm.private]. Add it (Keep email local). The related [llm.private] must be a model that runs on this machine, not one that sends text away means your private model is remote.

docs.title: sb ask finds nothing but you expect an answer
docs.text:
No encuentro nada sobre esto en la wiki.

The model cited no page that exists, or most sentences of its answer used numbers, names or words that are not in the pages it was given and cited (the check on the answer), so the answer was refused rather than guessed. With sb ask --json the second case still lists the sentences in unsupported. A small model does this more often; check_answers = false under [run] shows what the model said without the check. Try the words your notes use; turn on rewrite_questions or search by meaning; measure with sb eval. A different model in [llm.ask] can help (qwen3:4b cites the right page more often than llama3.2, but is about ten times slower).

docs.title: Embeddings are unavailable
docs.text:
warning: embeddings unavailable (...); searching by keyword only

[llm.embed] is set but Ollama cannot be reached or the model is not pulled (ollama pull nomic-embed-text). Search falls back to keywords; nothing breaks.

docs.title: Ticks are not registered
docs.text: Run sb index after ticking. The tick must be - [x] [[Source title]] on the line of the source, in a daily note under wiki/daily/. To undo a tick, untick the box in the note of the day the source was processed and run sb index: the source goes back to processed. A box unticked in any other day's note changes nothing. See Read your notes.

docs.title: The job stays running and never finishes
docs.text:
The log shows getcwd: Operation not permitted, or nothing at all. macOS privacy is waiting for, or has denied, access to ~/Documents. Click Allow on the dialog, or enable the Python framework under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Files & Folders. Then:

launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.esbi-cli.nightly

An agent cannot click that dialog for you. See Run it every night.

docs.title: sb doctor complains about the job
docs.text:
Line Meaning and fix WARN nightly job: not installed sb schedule install WARN nightly job: installed for 03:00 but config.toml says 04:30 Install again for the new time: sb schedule install WARN platform: esbi-cli is only supported on macOS for now (...) Not macOS. Nothing is promised there; it may work. See Other systems WARN nightly job: the nightly job uses launchd, which only macOS has Not macOS: add the line that sb schedule status prints to cron error: the nightly job uses launchd, which only macOS has You ran sb schedule install or uninstall where there is no launchd (not macOS, so not a supported system). sb schedule status prints the same advice but exits 0. The message includes the cron line to add with crontab -e; see cron WARN last run: no scheduled run yet The job has not run since you installed it The cron job never runs, and its log says sb: not found An old cron line that starts with a bare sb: cron's PATH is /usr/bin:/bin. Use the line sb schedule status prints now, which names sb by its absolute path The hourly check stops running batches before the queue is empty [run].max_batches_per_day (default 6) scheduled batches a day were reached, the nightly one included, or the latest scheduled batch stopped for a model outage or an interruption. The rest waits for the next night: raise max_batches_per_day under [run], or run sb run by hand WARN last run: DATE: the model server was unreachable (...) The latest run (manual or scheduled) stopped because the model was down. Nothing was lost. Start Ollama (brew services start ollama, or open the app) or fix the model line above it, then sb run. The hourly check retries by itself, and a run that reaches the model clears the warning. The daily index says the same, first under To review error: no .../bin/sb (run uv sync if this is a checkout) schedule install could not find sb in the running environment: reinstall it

Nothing happened overnight? Read <vault>/.esbi/logs/nightly.log. Not due: the nightly run already happened. is normal for the hourly checks when nothing is queued.

docs.title: Mail
docs.text: Messages from email capture, with fixes, are in Capture email. Which mail is taken and why a mail labelled late is still found: Which mail is taken. No keyring on a server or in WSL: Email where there is no keyring.

docs.title: Git and backup
docs.text: Message Meaning and fix warning: git commit failed: ... A commit failed (a git identity not set, a lock). The notes are written; fix git (git config user.name, user.email) and the next run commits warning: vault backup not pushed: ... The remote cannot be reached or refused the push. The run is fine; fix the remote (git -C VAULT remote -v) error: reingest rewrites every note and relies on the vault's git history to undo it; install git and run sb init first. sb reingest needs a git history: install git and run sb init History: git is not installed, so the vault has no version history. Optional. Install git and run sb init again error: ... is not an export of this wiki and has other files: not touching it sb export --out pointed at a folder that is not an export; pick an empty one

docs.title: Files, disks and unusual setups
docs.text:
These can happen on any system. Several show up most often where esbi-cli is not supported (a fresh Linux user, a container, WSL); they are listed because they were found and fixed there, not because those systems are supported.

Message or symptom Meaning and fix error: Permission denied: /path/to/file A file or folder could not be written: the vault is read-only, the disk is full, or the user has no permission. One line and exit 1, no traceback. With --json: {"error": ..., "code": "os_error"}. Fix the permission or free space, then run it again; nothing was lost error: the vault's state database cannot be used (...). Is the vault folder read-only, full or in use by another program? The queue or index database under .esbi/ cannot be opened or written. The same causes (read-only or full vault), or another program using it. It has the code os_error too error: this user has no home folder ($HOME is not set): give explicit paths (--vault, --config-file, --config) A container or service user with no home. sb version still starts, and a command that needs a home says so; give it the paths explicitly sb run \| head stops after a few lines Safe. The closed pipe stops the run quietly and the source being read goes back in the queue with no attempt counted, so it is never parked for it. Run it again A source with a very long title (Japanese, Chinese, Korean, emoji) was parked as failed with File name too long A page title is cut to 240 bytes (never inside a character), because some file systems (ext4, common on Linux) limit a file name to 255 bytes, not characters. A source parked for this goes back with sb retry Sources titled Foo and foo are one page (foo (2)), not two On purpose. A page or file name that differs from a taken one only by case, or only by Unicode form (é as one character or as e plus an accent), counts as taken, so a vault shared between a Mac and Linux never holds two names that a Mac sees as one. A re-read of the same address still updates its page Updated to X.Y.Z. Runsb versionto confirm. after sb update The upgrade changed the installed version, and the new one is named sb update prints Nothing changed: X.Y.Z is still installed. The command found nothing to upgrade (an exact version pin, or the new release is not on the package index yet: try again in a few minutes). The upgrade command exited 0 but changed nothing: a pinned install, or a release the package index does not list yet. Wait a few minutes and run sb update again, or reinstall by hand (Update esbi-cli) sb today prints the link but nothing opens The link is opened with open on macOS (xdg-open elsewhere, an unsupported system); otherwise open the link yourself. With [notes].viewer = "none" it prints the path sb export wrote nowhere you expected Without --out it writes to the site folder of the vault no keyring on this system Email capture needs a desktop keyring: Email where there is no keyring

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
The quick way is sb update: it shows the command for the way you installed esbi-cli, asks, and runs it. Update esbi-cli explains that and the notice that tells you a new version exists. By hand:

Read the changelog first: while the major version is 0, a minor version (0.4 to 0.5) may change a command or the config format, and it says so.

Installed with Update Homebrew brew update, then brew upgrade esbi-cli uv tool install git+... uv tool upgrade esbi-cli A wheel Download the new wheel, then uv tool install --force ~/Downloads/esbi_cli-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl A source checkout git pull in the folder; the change is live at once. After a new dependency, uv tool install --editable . --force

For a uv install the command prints what changed and ends with Nothing to upgrade when you are already current.

After an update, three commands:

sb version

sb doctor

sb schedule install
  • sb version shows the new version.
  • sb doctor shows anything the new version wants different.
  • sb schedule install (only if you use the nightly job) rewrites the job so it points at the sb that is installed now. It is safe to repeat, and it matters because the job remembers where sb lives. (With Homebrew the job points at a path that survives upgrades; sb doctor warns if yours was installed the old way. See Update esbi-cli.)

Your vault and config are not touched by an update. If a release says its notes have a new format, sb reingest rebuilds the old ones; see Manage the queue and old notes. The page index in .esbi/ is rebuilt by itself when its version changes.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
An uninstall removes the program. It does not touch your notes, and it leaves some small things behind on purpose. Do them in this order.

1. Remove the nightly job (macOS), while sb still exists:

sb schedule uninstall

Removed.

2. Remove the program:

brew uninstall esbi-cli

uv tool uninstall esbi-cli

Use the one that matches how you installed it. uv prints Uninstalled 1 executable: sb. Homebrew keeps the tap; remove it too with brew untap rubenamaury/esbi-cli. It also leaves Python 3.13, which other programs may use.

3. Decide what to do with what is left behind.

Left behind Where Remove it with Your vault, and its history The folder you chose, for example ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi Keep it: it is plain Markdown. To delete it, delete the folder The worker's state <vault>/.esbi/ (queue, page index, logs); disposable Goes with the vault. Delete the folder to start the queue afresh The config file ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml rm ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml The nightly job, if you forgot step 1 ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.esbi-cli.nightly.plist launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.esbi-cli.nightly, then delete the file The mailbox password The macOS Keychain, service esbi-cli-imap security delete-generic-password -s esbi-cli-imap -a you@gmail.com The Gmail side of email capture The esbi-cli label, its filter, the app password Delete the label and filter in Gmail, and revoke the app password at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords The models Ollama's store ollama rm llama3.2 (and any other you pulled) The Web Clipper setup Your browser, and Obsidian Remove the extension and the two templates in its settings The backup Your git remote Delete the repository there

Deleting the vault deletes your notes. The notes and the originals in raw/ live only in the vault (and its backup, if you made one). Everything else on this list is safe to delete.

docs.title: Update esbi-cli
docs.text: How you find out that a new version exists, and how to install it. Nothing updates by itself: you see a line, you run sb update, and it asks before it does anything.

docs.title: How you learn there is a new version
docs.text:
Three places tell you, and none of them slows a command down:

  • A line after a command. When you run a command in a terminal and a newer release is known, one line appears at the end, on stderr (so a pipe is not affected):

esbi-cli 0.2.0 is available (you have 0.1.0). Update with: sb update
