It never appears after sb run (the nightly job), sb schedule, sb update, sb setup, sb init, sb version or sb doctor, when the output goes to a file or a script instead of a terminal, or after a command that failed. - sb doctor has a version line: ok version: 0.1.0 (latest), or WARN version: 0.2.0 is available, runsb update`. - **sb version --check** asks right now and prints the installed and the latest version. A plainsb version` stays offline and instant.

The check asks GitHub at most once a day, remembers the answer in ~/.cache/esbi-cli/update.json ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/esbi-cli if you set it), and after a failure waits an hour before it tries again, so being offline costs nothing. It gives up after 5 seconds.

docs.title: Update with sb update
docs.text:
sb update

installed: 0.1.0
latest:    0.2.0
method:    brew
Will run: brew upgrade rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli
Run it now? [y/N]

It works out how esbi-cli was installed, shows the exact command and waits for a y. The command runs as it is shown, with no shell in between, and its output appears as it comes. When it ends successfully:

Updated to X.Y.Z. Run `sb version` to confirm.

It names the version that is installed afterwards. If the command ran and exited 0 but the installed version is the same (a uv tool pinned to an exact version, or a release the package index does not list yet), it does not pretend:

Nothing changed: X.Y.Z is still installed. The command found nothing to upgrade (an exact version pin, or the new release is not on the package index yet: try again in a few minutes).

Wait a few minutes and run sb update again, or update by hand (below).

Option Meaning --dry-run Only print the command --yes, -y Do not ask (for a script). Without a terminal and without --yes, sb update refuses and runs nothing

Read the changelog first when the minor version changes: while the major version is 0, it may change a command or the config format, and it says so.

docs.title: What it runs for each install method
docs.text: Installed with sb update runs Homebrew brew upgrade rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli uv tool install git+... uv tool upgrade esbi-cli pipx pipx upgrade esbi-cli pip in a virtual environment python -m pip install --upgrade <the release's archive on GitHub>, using the Python that runs sb A source checkout Nothing: it says git pull, then uv sync A uv tool pinned to a git tag or a wheel Nothing: uv tool upgrade cannot move a pinned install, so it prints the reinstall command to run Something it does not recognise Nothing: it lists the commands above

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
The same updates without sb update:

brew upgrade rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli

uv tool upgrade esbi-cli

pipx upgrade esbi-cli

A wheel from a GitHub release: download the new one, then uv tool install --force ~/Downloads/esbi_cli-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl. A source checkout: git pull, then uv sync (or uv tool install --editable . --force after a new dependency).

Afterwards, sb version shows the new version and sb doctor shows anything the new version wants different. Your vault and config are not touched.

docs.title: The nightly job keeps working
docs.text:
On macOS the nightly job is a launchd agent that remembers where sb lives. Homebrew keeps each version in its own folder (.../Cellar/esbi-cli/0.1.0/...) and deletes the old one on an upgrade, so a job that pointed there would stop. sb schedule install now writes the stable path Homebrew keeps pointing at the current version (.../opt/esbi-cli/libexec), and an upgrade needs nothing more.

If you installed the job with an older version, sb doctor shows WARN nightly job: points into a versioned Homebrew folder. Run sb schedule install once to fix it; it is safe to repeat.

docs.title: Turn the check off
docs.text:
In config.toml:

[update]
check = false

Or, in your shell profile, export ESBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1, which wins over the config. Then no line appears, sb doctor says (update check is off), and nothing asks GitHub. sb update and sb version --check still do, because you asked them to.

docs.title: What the check sends
docs.text:
One anonymous HTTPS GET to https://api.github.com/repos/RubenAmaury/esbi-cli/releases/latest, with a User-Agent that names esbi-cli and its version. No vault data, no config, no identifier of you or your machine. GitHub sees your IP address, as any website does. The answer is read as untrusted text: only the version tag and the release page address are used, and only when they have the expected shape. The scheduled run never checks. More on what leaves your machine: Safety and privacy.

To remove the program, see Update and uninstall.

docs.title: Use it offline
docs.text: With a local model, esbi-cli can do almost everything without a network. What needs one is fetching, not thinking.

docs.title: What works with no network
docs.text:
With a local model (Ollama or LM Studio on this machine) and the models already downloaded:

Works offline How Notes from PDFs, Markdown clips and images Drop them in inbox/, or sb add file, then sb run Reading, ticking, the daily index sb today, sb index Asking questions sb ask, with the keyword search or hybrid search (the embedding model is local) Lint, evaluation, sb reingest sb lint, sb eval, sb reingest (it reads from raw/, so it needs no internet) Backup to a drive or NAS A git remote on your network, or a folder copy Browsing the wiki sb export; everything works except the concept diagrams, which load a library from a CDN The nightly job It runs on your machine

docs.title: What needs a network
docs.text: Needs the network Why sb add URL and sb run of a link The page has to be fetched. A link queued offline fails (Could not fetch ...) and is retried on later runs: after three tries it is parked, and sb retry puts it back Email capture IMAP to Gmail A cloud model (API, Claude or ChatGPT subscription) The model is elsewhere. When it cannot be reached the run stops and nothing is lost; a fallback local model takes over if you set one Downloading a model, installing, updating Once Pushing the backup to GitHub or another remote A failed push is only a warning The concept diagrams in an exported site The page loads Mermaid from a CDN

docs.title: A plan for a flight
docs.text:
Before you go: pull the models you need (ollama list), sb run so the queue is empty, and put the PDFs you want to read in inbox/ or save the pages you want as Markdown clips while you are still online (a clip is read from its own text; the worker never fetches it again). In the air: sb run writes their notes, and sb ask works.

If you use a cloud model normally, set a local fallback so the run does not stop when the network goes:

[llm.summarize]
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

Details: Choose how the notes are written.

docs.title: Web Clipper and YouTube
docs.text: The Obsidian Web Clipper is a browser extension that saves what you see as a Markdown file. It is the way to get in pages behind a login, LinkedIn, X and Reddit posts, and YouTube transcripts: the worker never scrapes those, and the clipped text is the source. It is optional, and it needs Obsidian.

docs.title: Set it up with the wizard
docs.text:
sb setup clipper

The wizard has five stages:

  1. Install the extension for your browser and pin it to the toolbar.
  2. Add your vault to the Clipper's settings, by the vault's folder name.
  3. Import the template clipper-template.json. It saves into inbox/ with the properties title, source (the page URL), author, published and kind: article. The wizard also tells you about the YouTube template (below).
  4. Clip a test page (the wizard opens one).
  5. Run sb scan to check the worker reads the clip.

If your config says viewer = "none" the wizard says so and stops: the Clipper saves into an Obsidian vault.

docs.title: Use it
docs.text:
Clip a page with the extension. The next sb run, or tonight's run, turns it into a note. The clip is not fetched again: whatever you saw is what is read, which is why this works for pages that need a login.

To queue clips without running everything: sb scan.

docs.title: What is removed from a clip
docs.text: Clips of GitHub, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Reddit and YouTube pages come with the site's menus, sign-in prompts, cookie lines, sidebars, share bars and footers. Before the model reads the clip, the worker removes the lines that are known page chrome, so the note summarises the post or article and not the menu. Only whole lines that are known chrome are removed (never a sentence that contains such words, never code, plain bullets or transcript rows), and a clip from any other site is not touched. The original stays in raw/inbox/; the note's stripped_lines: N and the run's warning tell you how many lines were taken out. A clip that was nothing but chrome is rejected as having almost no text. Details: Add a Markdown clip.

docs.title: YouTube videos with a transcript
docs.text:
Import the second template, clipper-youtube-template.json. It applies by itself on youtube.com/watch pages. Open a video that has a transcript and clip it.

The note is written like any other, from the transcript, and every quote and glossary term that the transcript contains carries a link that opens the video at that second: ([2:20](https://youtube.com/watch?v=...&t=140s)). The transcript is whatever language the Clipper gets from YouTube (often English, even for a Spanish video); the note is written in the language of [notes].language. A video without a transcript cannot be processed this way. The worker never downloads video or audio.

docs.title: Without the Clipper
docs.text: Any tool that saves a page as a Markdown file with title: and source: (the URL) at the top works the same if you drop its files in inbox/. See Add a Markdown clip.

docs.title: Use it without Obsidian
docs.text: The vault is plain Markdown folders (frontmatter, [[links]], - [ ] checkboxes), so any editor can read and edit it: VS Code, Logseq, Typora, or just a text editor. Obsidian is only the viewer, and nothing here needs it.

docs.title: Turn it off
docs.text:
Set viewer = "none" under [notes] in config.toml, or answer no to the Obsidian question in sb init (or run sb init --no-obsidian):

[notes]
viewer = "none"

What changes:

  • sb today prints the path of today's note instead of opening an obsidian:// link, and sb doctor stops asking you to open the folder in Obsidian.
  • sb setup clipper explains that the Web Clipper needs Obsidian and stops.

docs.title: Read and tick
docs.text:
Open today's note with any editor:

sb today

~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

Ticking works the same: put an x in - [ ] in the daily note with your editor, save, and run sb index. See Read your notes and tick what you have read. The [[links]] are Obsidian's wiki-link syntax; other editors show them as text, and some (Logseq, Foam, VS Code with a wiki-link extension) follow them.

docs.title: Browse as a website
docs.text:
sb export

writes a read-only website of the wiki for any browser: Export a website.

docs.title: Get sources in
docs.text: sb add URL, dropping PDFs and Markdown files in inbox/, and email all work without Obsidian. The Web Clipper is an Obsidian project and needs it; another tool that saves a page as a Markdown file with title: and source: (the URL) at the top works the same if you drop its files in inbox/. See Get sources in.

docs.title: Run it every night
docs.text: Nothing needs Obsidian: Run it every night.

docs.title: What you give up
docs.text: The graph view, backlinks panel and live search of Obsidian. The questions you would ask them, you can ask the wiki: sb ask "..." (Ask your wiki).

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
Every command of sb, with every option, its default, what it prints and how it exits. sb --help and sb <command> --help print the same list; this page adds what the help text has no room for. For a task ("how do I add a PDF?") start from How do I...?.

Examples show the default vault, ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi. Your paths will differ.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• --config PATH. Every command that reads the config accepts it. When it is left out, the file is found as described in Configuration. sb version, sb update, sb schedule status, sb schedule uninstall and sb init do not read a config (sb init writes one: --config-file). A --config path that does not exist is an error (error: config file not found: PATH), not a reason to use another file. A config whose [paths].vault folder does not exist is an error too (error: vault not found: PATH (runsb init, or fix [paths].vault), --json code vault_not_found) for every command that opens the vault: nothing is created. sb doctor, sb init and the commands that only edit the config (sb ocr ..., sb email set-password) still work.
  • Exit codes. 0 is success. 1 is an error the command already explained on the screen (a missing config, a bad argument, the model is down, a FAIL line in sb doctor). 2 is a usage mistake caught by the command-line parser (an unknown command or option); it prints the usage and a hint. 130 and 143 are a stop you asked for: Ctrl-C (SIGINT) and SIGTERM, the conventional 128 plus the signal number. They come from sb run, sb ingest and sb reingest; see Stopping a command. A file or disk problem (a read-only or full vault, a missing permission, a vault's state database that cannot be used, a user with no home folder) is one line, error: Permission denied: /path for example, with exit 1 and no traceback (--json: code os_error). A closed output pipe (sb run | head) stops quietly and puts the source being read back in the queue, with no attempt counted.
  • --json. sb version, status, info, doctor, add, ask and run accept --json and then print JSON for a program to read instead of text. The shapes are in JSON output.
  • Quote what the shell would read. A URL with ? or & must be in quotes, or zsh answers no matches found before sb starts: sb add "https://example.com/post?id=7".
  • Shell completion. sb --install-completion installs it for the current shell, sb --show-completion prints the script to copy.

docs.title: Commands at a glance
docs.text: Command What it does sb A numbered menu of everyday actions sb init First-time setup: the vault, a config file, the optional pieces sb doctor Check the whole setup and say what to fix sb info Print where the config and the vault are, as key=value lines sb version Print the installed version; --check looks for a newer one sb update Update esbi-cli to the latest release (asks first) sb add Queue links or files for the next run sb scan Queue what is in inbox/ sb status Queue counts and sources that failed sb retry Put failed sources back in the queue sb drop Remove a source from the queue sb run The main job: mail, inbox, queue, summaries, lint, index sb ingest Ingest one source right now sb reingest Rebuild notes from the saved originals sb consolidate Write a consolidated summary on concept and entity pages sb import-legacy One-time import of an older folder of links and PDFs sb today Open (or print the path of) today's daily note sb index Register read ticks, rebuild the daily index sb lint Check the wiki's health sb ask Answer a question from the wiki sb eval Score retrieval on your own questions sb bench Compare models on your own material sb export Write a read-only HTML copy of the wiki sb ocr status, enable, disable Read images and scanned PDFs with a local vision model (optional) sb setup email, sb setup clipper Guided setups for Gmail capture and the Web Clipper sb email fetch, configure, set-password Mail capture sb schedule install, status, uninstall The nightly job (macOS launchd)

docs.title: Stopping a command
docs.text: Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during sb run, sb ingest or sb reingest stops it cleanly. A note is never cut in half: a signal that arrives while a note and its pages are being written waits until they are whole, then the command stops. The source that was being read goes back to the queue without counting an attempt (three interruptions no longer park a good source), the command exits with 130 (Ctrl-C) or 143 (SIGTERM), and says Interrupted: 1 item put back in the queue. (N items for more, on stderr). sb ingest and sb reingest say Interrupted.; sb reingest resumes where it stopped. An interrupted scheduled run does not count as tonight's nightly run, so the job tries again.

docs.title: sb (menu)
docs.text:
sb

With no command, a numbered menu. Each choice runs the real command, asking for what it needs, prints its output and returns to the menu. A mistake or a failing command never closes it.

esbi-cli
  1. Queue status
  2. Run now (ingest what is queued)
  3. Ask the wiki a question
  4. Add links or files to the queue
  5. Open today's note in Obsidian
  6. Check the wiki's health (lint)
  7. Check my setup (doctor)
Choose (q to quit) [q]: 1
queued: 1
processing: 0
done: 1
failed: 0

Anything else than a number from 1 to 7 or q prints Not an option. The menu has no --config: it uses the usual search (set ESBI_CONFIG to point it elsewhere).

docs.title: sb init
docs.text:
sb init [--vault PATH] [--config-file PATH] [--model local|subscription|api]
        [--runtime ollama|lmstudio] [--local-model NAME] [--base-url URL]
        [--language en|es] [--obsidian | --no-obsidian] [--nightly HH:MM|none] [--remote URL]
        [--ocr | --no-ocr] [--ocr-model NAME] [--pull-ocr-model]

First-time setup. It creates the vault if it is missing, writes a config file and says what to do next. When git is installed it makes the vault a repository and a first commit (init: vault), so the vault's .gitignore, which keeps .esbi/ out, is tracked from the start; a commit that fails does not fail the setup. It only creates what is missing: running it again changes nothing that exists and never overwrites a config.

At a keyboard it is an installer that asks one question per setting; with no keyboard (a script, a pipe) it asks nothing and uses the flag, or the default. The walk-through, with what each answer changes, is in Getting started.

Option Default Meaning --vault PATH ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi Where the vault lives. Created if missing --config-file PATH ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml Where the config is written. An existing file is left alone --model local (no keyboard) local: a model on this machine, nothing leaves it. subscription: your Claude subscription through the official claude tool, with a local fallback. api: Anthropic's API, billed per token (set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). The last two keep email on the local model --runtime ollama Which local runtime: ollama or lmstudio. Also the failsafe for subscription and api --local-model NAME llama3.2:latest for Ollama The local model's name. Required for lmstudio (see lms ls) --base-url URL this machine Only with --model local: the address of an Ollama or LM Studio server that is not on this Mac. The notes' text then goes to that host, so sb init warns and sb doctor keeps warning --language en (no keyboard) The language the notes are written in, en or es: written as [notes].language, and used for the vault's SCHEMA.md and index.md. The command line itself is always English. See Language of the notes --obsidian / --no-obsidian --obsidian (no keyboard), no (asked) Writes viewer = "obsidian" or viewer = "none" in [notes] --nightly HH:MM or none none Run every night at that time: installs the launchd job on macOS, prints a cron line elsewhere (with sb by absolute path). Only when the config is new: an existing config is left alone, and so is the job --remote URL none Connects the vault to a git remote for backup (an existing remote is never replaced). Needs git --ocr / --no-ocr --no-ocr (asked at a keyboard, default No) Also writes an [llm.ocr] section so images and scanned PDFs are read. Needs --runtime ollama --ocr-model NAME the best model this machine's memory allows Which Ollama vision model reads images. Goes with --ocr. A name that is not a plausible Ollama model name is refused --pull-ocr-model off Download the vision model now if Ollama does not have it, showing progress (an interrupted download resumes). Goes with --ocr. Without this flag, or a typed yes at a keyboard, nothing is downloaded

The images question. At a keyboard, after the backup remote, sb init asks Read images and scanned PDFs (jpg, png, ...)? It needs a local vision model. The default is No: reading images is optional and nothing is downloaded unless you say so. On yes it lists the known vision models with their download size and the memory each wants, marks the one that suits this machine, and lets you type any other Ollama model. qwen3-vl:2b-instruct (1.9 GB) is the recommended model and fits an 8 GB Mac; deepseek-ocr:3b (6.7 GB) is a choice for a machine with 16 GB of memory or more (on an 8 GB Mac it was measured unusable, about 100 times slower). It then says whether Ollama already has the model and, if not, asks Download it now? (default No). It never blocks on a small machine: it only warns. The question is skipped with --runtime lmstudio, and when the config already exists it is left alone (sb ocr enable changes it).

Errors it reports and exits 1 on: an unknown --model, --runtime or --language, --runtime lmstudio without --local-model, --ocr with LM Studio, --ocr-model or --pull-ocr-model without --ocr, --base-url with a cloud model or without a host, a --nightly that is not HH:MM.

sb init --vault ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi --model local --no-obsidian

Vault ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi: inbox/, raw/, attachments/, wiki/sources/, wiki/concepts/, wiki/entities/, wiki/syntheses/, wiki/review/, wiki/daily/, SCHEMA.md, index.md, log.md, .gitignore, git repository
Config ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml: written
Model: local. Everything stays on this Mac: the notes are written by a local model.

Next: ollama pull llama3.2, then sb doctor. Add a link with `sb add URL` or drop a PDF in the vault's inbox/ folder.

Without git installed the vault is created without history and the message History: git is not installed, so the vault has no version history... appears. It does not install Ollama or pull a model.

docs.title: sb doctor
docs.text:
sb doctor [--config PATH] [--json]

Checks the whole setup and prints one line per check, with the fix under anything that is not fine. ok is fine, WARN is an inconvenience, FAIL is broken. Exit code 1 only when a line is FAIL.

  ok   config: ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml
  ok   version: 0.1.0 (latest)
  ok   vault: ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi
  ok   obsidian: not used ([notes].viewer = "none")
  ok   queue: empty
  WARN last run: no scheduled run yet
         fix: the job does it after the nightly time; or try `sb run --if-due`
  ok   model summarize: ollama/llama3.2:latest is installed
  ok   ocr: off (optional): `sb ocr enable` turns on reading images and scanned PDFs with a local vision model ([llm.ocr], https://rubenamaury.github.io/esbi-cli/docs/reference/configuration/)
  ok   email privacy: all models are local
  ok   email: off (optional)
  WARN nightly job: not installed
         fix: sb schedule install
  ok   global install: /opt/homebrew/bin/sb
Check Looks at config Which config.toml applies, and that it is valid: a misspelled key, an unknown section or a value of the wrong type is a FAIL naming the setting version The installed version, and a WARN (0.2.0 is available, runsb update`) when a newer release is known. It reads the once-a-day cache and asks GitHub only when that is stale; if GitHub cannot be reached the line is just the version, and with[update].check = falseit says(update check is off)` platform Only off macOS: WARN platform: esbi-cli is only supported on macOS for now (<system> is not supported: it may work, nothing is promised). Nothing else changes; the other checks run as usual. macOS shows no line vault The folder has SCHEMA.md and wiki/ vault history Whether the vault is a git repository (a warning only when git is installed but the vault is not a repository) obsidian The folder was opened once as a vault in Obsidian (.obsidian exists); with viewer = "none" it just says not used queue Queue counts; warns when sources failed for good last run The last scheduled run. WARN with the time and the model server was unreachable (nothing was lost; the sources stay queued) when the latest run, scheduled or manual, stopped because the model could not be reached: start Ollama or check the model, then sb run. A later run that reached the model clears it model <task> For each of summarize, synthesize, ask, private, embed that is set (and its fallback): Ollama is reachable and the model installed, LM Studio serves the model, claude is installed and logged in (claude auth status), codex is installed and logged in (codex login status), or the API key is in the environment ocr, model ocr Images and scanned PDFs are off (ok, optional; it says when a model choice is kept), or [llm.ocr] is not a model on this machine (FAIL), or the vision model is installed (and FAIL with the exact ollama pull command when it is not) ocr memory WARN only when reading is on with a known model and this machine has less memory than that model wants (for example deepseek-ocr:3b on 8 GB); the fix names the recommended model ocr ollama WARN only when the Ollama that serves the vision model is older than the one the model needs (brew upgrade ollama, or update the app) email privacy Email is read only by a local model; warns when a cloud model is set with no [llm.private]; fails when [llm.private] sends text away server <task> Warns when an Ollama or LM Studio model is served from another machine network Only when [network] use_environment_proxy = true: WARN, because the address checks are then the proxy's, not esbi-cli's (fix: set it to false unless this network only has a proxy) email Only when enabled: the app password is in the Keychain (off macOS, which is not supported, the system keyring: a server, a container or WSL has none, see Email where there is no keyring) nightly job The launchd job is installed, loaded and set for the time in the config, and does not point into a versioned Homebrew folder (Cellar) that brew upgrade deletes (fix: sb schedule install). Off macOS it is a WARN: launchd only exists on macOS, and the fix is the cron line that sb schedule status prints global install sb is on your PATH. When it is not, the fix: line matches how esbi-cli was installed: brew upgrade rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli, uv tool upgrade esbi-cli, pipx upgrade esbi-cli or pip install -U esbi-cli; uv tool install --editable <folder> only appears for a source checkout

With --json it prints one object with ok and every check (see JSON output); the exit code is the same.

Every message and its fix are listed by symptom in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: sb info
docs.text:
sb info [--config PATH] [--json]

Prints where things are, as key=value lines. The setup wizards read it; it is also the quickest answer to "which config is it using?".

config=~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml
vault=~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi
viewer=none
language=en
email=disabled

With --json it prints the same facts, the models per task, whether each of them sends text out, and the nightly job as one object: see JSON output.

docs.title: sb version
docs.text:
sb version [--check] [--json]

Prints the installed version, for example 0.1.0. It reads the package metadata, so it is the version that is installed, not the one in a checkout. Without options it is offline and instant.

--check also asks GitHub for the latest release (one anonymous HTTPS request, ignoring the once-a-day cache) and prints one more line: You are up to date., or the new version and Update with: sb update. If GitHub cannot be reached it says so and still exits 0.

--json prints {"contract":1,"version":"0.3.0"} and nothing else (--check does not ask GitHub then): it is how a program learns which version, and which JSON contract, it is talking to.

docs.title: sb update
docs.text:
sb update [--yes] [--dry-run]

Updates esbi-cli to the latest release. It asks GitHub for it (ignoring the once-a-day cache), prints the installed version, the latest version and how esbi-cli was installed (brew, uv-tool, pipx, pip, editable or unknown), then the exact command it will run and Run it now? [y/N]. Nothing is installed without that yes.

Option Meaning --yes, -y Do not ask; run the command --dry-run Only print the command; run nothing

Without a terminal and without --yes it refuses (exit 1) and runs nothing. The command is run without a shell and its output is shown as it comes. On success it prints Updated to X.Y.Z. Run `sb version` to confirm. with the version that is now installed. If the command exits 0 but the installed version did not change (a uv tool pinned to an exact version, or a release the package index does not list yet) it says so instead: Nothing changed: X.Y.Z is still installed. The command found nothing to upgrade (an exact version pin, or the new release is not on the package index yet: try again in a few minutes). It does not claim an update that did not happen. if the command fails it exits with that command's code. When there is no command to run (a source checkout, an unknown install, or a uv tool pinned to a git ref or a wheel) it prints what to do by hand. When you are already current it says so. See Update esbi-cli.

docs.title: sb add
docs.text:
sb add TARGET... [--config PATH] [--json]

Queues one or several sources for the next sb run. Nothing is fetched now. A target is an http(s) URL, or the path to an existing .pdf or .md file, or an image (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .tif, .tiff) when [llm.ocr] is set; without it the error says how to turn it on.

If any target is invalid nothing is queued and the bad ones are listed (exit 1). A link must have a host and no spaces or line breaks, so several links passed as one argument (sb add "$LINKS", a paste) are refused: pass each link as its own argument. Tracking parameters, letter case and a trailing slash are ignored. A link already in the queue is counted as already known; a link already in the wiki is skipped and the note that has it is named. The rules for every kind of duplicate are in If a source already exists. A .md clip added from outside the vault's inbox/ (sb add clip.md) is read from where it is; when its note is written the original is copied unchanged into raw/inbox/ (clip (2).md if the name is taken), so it is kept the same as a clip dropped in inbox/.

sb add https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten

Queued 1 (0 already known). `sb run` processes them.

sb add notaurl

error: not an http(s) URL or an existing .pdf/.md file:
  notaurl

With --json the result is one object (queued, already_known, in_wiki), and a bad target is an error object with the code bad_target: see JSON output.

docs.title: sb scan
docs.text:
sb scan [--config PATH]

Queues what is waiting in the vault's inbox/: .md clips and .pdf files, and images when [llm.ocr] is set. Each file is moved to raw/inbox/, its permanent home, and queued from there. sb run does this for you; run sb scan by itself to see the queue before a run.

  • A byte-identical copy of a file already in raw/inbox/ (under any name) is a duplicate: it is removed from inbox/, counted and not queued.
  • A different file with the same name is kept under a new name (paper (2).pdf). Nothing in raw/ is ever overwritten.
  • Hidden files and folders are skipped.
  • Any other file that cannot be read stays where it is and is listed: Not read, esbi-cli cannot read these files in inbox/: ..., with the way to turn OCR on when an image is among them.
Queued 1 sources from the inbox.

docs.title: sb status
docs.text:
sb status [--config PATH] [--json]

Prints the number of sources queued, processing, done and failed, then one line per source that failed for good with its last error. A source still being retried (it failed once or twice) counts as queued; its last error is in the daily note under To review.

queued: 2
processing: 0
done: 0
failed: 1
  failed: https://example.com/ (ExtractError: No readable article content found at https://example.com/)

With --json it prints the counts, the parked sources and the ones still being retried, each with its attempts and last error: see JSON output.

docs.title: sb retry
docs.text:
sb retry [TARGET] [--config PATH]

Puts sources that failed three times (parked as failed) back in the queue with a fresh attempt count, so the next sb run tries them again. Without TARGET it requeues every parked source; with one (a URL or path as sb status shows it; tracking parameters are ignored) only that one.

Requeued 1 source.

When nothing is parked it prints Nothing to retry. and exits 0.

docs.title: sb drop
docs.text:
sb drop TARGET [--config PATH]

Removes a source from the queue whatever its state (queued, retrying, failed or done). The original file, if there is one, is not touched, and a note already written stays. You can add the source again later. If TARGET is not in the queue: error: <target> is not in the queue, exit 1.

Dropped https://example.com/

docs.title: sb run
docs.text:
sb run [--config PATH] [--limit N] [--if-due] [--json]

The whole pipeline, in this order:

  1. Fetch mail from the mailbox (only if [email].enabled; a mail problem is a warning, never fatal). With [email].follow_links the links in new mail are queued here, not fetched.
  2. Scan inbox/ and queue what is there.
  3. Put back in the queue anything a crashed run had claimed.
  4. Ingest queued sources one by one; every success is a git commit in the vault.
  5. Record the run.
  6. Write consolidated summaries for the pages this run touched that are due, up to [run].max_consolidations_per_run (0, off, by default: see sb consolidate). Skipped after an outage.
  7. Lint the wiki.
  8. Register your read ticks, rebuild the daily index and Home.md, push the vault to its remote if it has one.
Option Default Meaning --limit N [run].max_sources_per_run (20) Ingest at most N sources this run --if-due off Scheduled mode: run only when a scheduled batch is due, and otherwise print Not due: the nightly run already happened. A batch is due when today's nightly run has not happened yet, or when it has and sources are queued, whatever ended the last batch (max_sources_per_run, max_tokens_per_run, max_usd_per_run, or an empty queue that filled again): the hourly tick then drains the queue, one batch per tick, and no more than [run].max_batches_per_day scheduled batches a day, default 6, counted from nightly_time and including the nightly run, which is what bounds a day's spend (a run that stopped for an outage or an interruption, and a manual run, do not count). Never after a scheduled run that stopped for an outage or an interruption (that waits for the next night, or is retried as described in Run it every night), and never while another run is active. Manual runs never count --json off Print one JSON object per line (JSON Lines) for a program to read, instead of the progress text: started, source_started, step, source_done, source_failed, finished. Flushed line by line. See JSON output

A run stops early when it reaches max_sources_per_run, max_tokens_per_run or max_usd_per_run (an estimate: tokens times the model's price in [bench.prices]; models on this machine and claude-cli or codex-cli count as 0, see [run]); what is left stays queued, with no attempt counted, and the run is recorded as max_sources, token_budget or usd_budget. A source that fails is retried on later runs (three attempts, then it is parked as failed). Every failure is reported on its own line, before the summary, with the source (its title if it has one, else its link or path), which attempt it was and a short reason; a source that has used all its attempts says it is parked and that sb retry puts it back. The summary line counts them (failed: 1). The full error is in sb status once the source is parked, and in the daily note under To review (Por revisar with language = "es"), which also lists the sources still being retried. Only one run can be active at a time.

Exit codes. 0 when the run finished or stopped early on a limit, and also when another run holds the lock (it prints Another run is in progress; skipping.) or --if-due found nothing due (Not due: the nightly run already happened.). 1 when the model is unreachable: nothing is counted against the sources, the index is still rebuilt, and the message is The LLM is unreachable (is Ollama running?). Nothing was lost; sources stay queued. 1 also for a config error, such as an unknown provider in model. 130 after Ctrl-C and 143 after SIGTERM: the source being read went back to the queue with no attempt counted, no lint or index is built, and the message on stderr is Interrupted: 1 item put back in the queue. (see Stopping a command).

sb run

    ... chunk 1 of 5
    ... chunk 2 of 5
    ... chunk 3 of 5
    ... chunk 4 of 5
    ... chunk 5 of 5
    ... synthesis
    ... detailed summary
    ... connections
  + Zettelkasten
    ... synthesis
    ... connections
  + Spaced Repetition
ingested: 2, skipped: 0, failed: 0 (20826 tokens)
Lint: 2 issues (see wiki/review/Lint.md)
Wrote wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

A failure looks like this (the same source on its first and its third run):

  ! http://localhost:9/old-page: attempt 1 of 3 failed, will be tried again: ExtractError: Refused to fetch http://localhost:9/old-page: localhost resolves to a non-public address (127.0.0.1)
  ! http://localhost:9/old-page: attempt 3 of 3 failed, parked (`sb retry` puts it back): ExtractError: Refused to fetch http://localhost:9/old-page: localhost resolves to a non-public address (127.0.0.1)

The reason is cut to one line of at most 160 characters. The lines starting ... are steps of the source being read: chunk N of M is chunk N of M being read, synthesis the core note, detailed summary the abstract (long sources), connections the links to your other notes. A line with + is a source written. Warnings (a repaired one-liner, a dropped entity, a skipped chunk, Only half of chunk 2 of 5 could be read., Dropped 2 diagram edges: an end was not in the source or the note.) follow it.

docs.title: sb ingest
docs.text:
sb ingest TARGET [--config PATH] [--force] [--dry-run] [--no-commit]

Ingests one source immediately, bypassing the queue and the run lock. TARGET is an http(s) URL, or the path to a PDF, a Markdown note (a Web Clipper clip) or an image. A clip from outside the vault's inbox/ is copied unchanged into raw/inbox/ when its note is written (name (2).md if the name is taken; the same applies to a clip queued by sb add and read by sb run), because the snapshot raw/<date>-<slug>.md holds the text after the page chrome was stripped.

Option Default Meaning --force off Ingest even if the same URL or the same text is already in the vault --dry-run off Print the model's edit plan as JSON and write nothing --no-commit off Write the files but do not commit them to the vault's git history

A source already in the vault is skipped: Already in the vault as [[...]] (use --force to redo). After a successful ingest it prints the title and the pages created: and updated:, how many notes went to wiki/review/, references to unknown pages that were ignored, and entities dropped because their name is not in the source. Errors (an unreadable source, the model down, a refused URL) print error: ... and exit 1. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops it cleanly (Interrupted., exit 130 or 143): see Stopping a command. When the ingest makes a concept or entity page due for a summary, it is written at the end, up to [run].max_consolidations_per_run.

sb ingest ~/Documents/clips/active-recall.md

... synthesis
... connections
Ingested: Active recall versus rereading
  created:  Active recall versus rereading, Active Recall, Rereading
  updated:  -
  ignored references to unknown pages: Spaced Repetition
  dropped entities not found in the source: Roland Barthes
  committed to the vault repo

docs.title: sb reingest
docs.text:
sb reingest [TITLE...] [--config PATH] [--all]

Rebuilds source notes from their originals in raw/ with the current pipeline. It is how notes written by an older version, or by a weaker model, are upgraded; it needs no network (PDFs are read again so their figures come back).

Argument / option Meaning TITLE... Only the notes whose title contains one of these words, whatever their format --all Rebuild every note again, even those already in the current format (format: 2) (neither) Every note that is not yet in the current format

What it keeps and what it replaces:

  • Language: the note is rebuilt in the language [notes].language names now, so sb reingest --all is how old notes follow a change of language. Notes you do not rebuild keep theirs.
  • Kept: the note's title (so every [[link]] to it stays valid), status, read, captured, content_hash, and the tags you added.
  • Replaced: the ## From [[...]] (or ## Desde [[...]], whatever language it was written in) sections the old note added to concept and entity pages are removed and written again; a concept page nobody else cites is deleted.
  • Undo: before touching anything the vault is committed and tagged pre-reingest-YYYY-MM-DD. git -C <vault> reset --hard pre-reingest-YYYY-MM-DD brings everything back.
  • Resumable: a rebuilt note is marked format: 2. If the run stops (the model went away, the Mac slept, Ctrl-C or SIGTERM, which end it with Interrupted. and exit 130 or 143), run the command again and it continues. A signal never leaves a note half-rewritten: the note's read state is not lost either.
  • One git commit per note. A note whose original is missing in raw/ is skipped and listed; a note that fails is listed and the rest go on.
  • It takes the run lock: it will not start while sb run works (Another run is in progress; try again when it finishes., exit 1), and the nightly job skips its turn while it runs.
  • It refuses to run without git: error: reingest rewrites every note and relies on the vault's git history to undo it; install git and run sb init first.

Expect minutes per source with a small local model.

[1/1] Active recall versus rereading
    ... synthesis
    ... connections
Vault tagged pre-reingest-2026-10-03 (undo: git -C ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi reset --hard pre-reingest-2026-10-03)
rebuilt: 1, skipped: 0, failed: 0

docs.title: sb consolidate
docs.text:
sb consolidate [--config PATH] [--all] [--only TITLE ...] [--dry-run]

Writes a consolidated ## Summary (## Resumen with language = "es") at the top of concept and entity pages, from the ## From [[source]] sections the page already has. The summary says what the concept is and what the sources add up to; the sections stay below it as the evidence. It is the manual twin of the automatic pass that sb run and sb ingest do for the pages they just wrote (up to [run].max_consolidations_per_run, which is 0, off, by default). This command has no cap.

Without options it takes the pages with three or more sources and no summary yet, or two or more sources since the last one. Each page costs one model call (two when the first answer fails its checks).

Option Default Meaning --all off Every concept and entity page with two or more sources, not only the due ones --only TITLE none Only pages whose title contains this word, ignoring case and accents. Repeat it for several --dry-run off List the pages that would be summarised and the number of sources each has; ask no model, write nothing

What it checks before the page changes: the summary has 80 to 900 characters, no links, URLs or HTML, is in the notes' language, and states nothing the sections do not (a quoted phrase, a number, a capitalised name that is not in them). A failing summary is retried once. A second failure leaves the page as it was and writes the proposal to wiki/review/ as <page> - summary to review (<page> - resumen por revisar), with the reasons, for you to check. A page that email helped write is summarised only by [llm.private] or a model on this machine; if there is none, the page is skipped and listed. Pages that look like the same idea (same name ignoring case and accents, plural and singular, an acronym and its expansion, very similar titles) get a note <page> - possible merge (posible fusión) in wiki/review/: nothing is ever merged for you.

One git commit per page. It takes the run lock: while sb run works it says Another run is in progress; try again when it finishes. and exits 1. If the model goes away it stops with exit 1 (The LLM is unreachable (is Ollama running?). Nothing was lost: runsb consolidateagain.) and the next run continues with the pages still due.

[1/2] Agent harness
[2/2] Context window
consolidated: 2, skipped: 0, to review: 0, merge suggestions: 1

With nothing to do it prints Nothing to consolidate. Why the cap is off by default, and what to read first: Consolidated summaries.

docs.title: sb import-legacy
docs.text:
sb import-legacy [--config PATH]

Queues every URL in an older folder's Links/*.md files (one [url] per line, oldest file first) and every PDF in its PDFs/ folder. It needs [paths].legacy_vault in the config; without it: error: set [paths].legacy_vault to an existing folder (exit 1). It never changes the old folder and is safe to repeat: known sources are counted as already known. The date of each links file becomes the note's captured date.

Queued 5 sources (0 already known).

Run again, it says Queued 0 sources (5 already known).

docs.title: sb today
docs.text:
sb today [--config PATH]

Opens today's daily note. If the note does not exist yet it is built first. With viewer = "obsidian" it prints and opens an obsidian://open link (Obsidian must know the vault: open the folder once as a vault). The link is opened with open on macOS and xdg-open elsewhere; with no such command the link is printed with a note to open it yourself. With viewer = "none" it only prints the file's path, for any editor.

~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

docs.title: sb index
docs.text:
sb index [--config PATH]

Registers the sources you ticked in earlier daily notes (they become status: read), puts a read source back to processed when you unticked its box in the note of the day it was processed, then rewrites today's wiki/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md and the managed block of Home.md, commits, and pushes to the vault's remote if it has one. It is cheap and needs no model: run it whenever you want the index refreshed. The sections of the note are in The daily index.

Marked 1 source as read.
Wrote wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

An unticked box prints Put 1 source back to unread. (Put 2 sources back to unread.). Only the box in the daily note of the day the source was processed counts, and only when it is unticked there and ticked nowhere else in that note; a source with no box in that note is left as it is. sb run does the same before it rebuilds the index.

docs.title: sb lint
docs.text:
sb lint [--config PATH]

Deterministic checks with no model. Prints a count per kind and writes wiki/review/Lint.md, which appears under To review in the daily note. The file exists only while there is something to fix. It only reports; it never edits the wiki.

Kind Meaning orphan No other page links to this one broken-link A [[link]] to a page that does not exist missing-field A page without title or summary unlinked-mention A concept's name appears in a page that does not link to it. Multi-word names match ignoring case and accents; a single word only matches exactly as written near-duplicate Two concepts or entities that look like the same idea (plural or accent variants, singular and plural such as Red/Redes, an acronym and its expansion such as IA/Inteligencia artificial, a shared alias) missing-concept A glossary term that two or more source notes define, with no concept or entity page of its own 
unlinked-mention: 1
near-duplicate: 1
Details in wiki/review/Lint.md

With nothing to report it prints No problems found.

docs.title: sb ask
docs.text:
sb ask "QUESTION" [--config PATH] [--save] [--json]

Answers from the wiki only. It finds the relevant pages with full-text search (and by meaning too, when [llm.embed] is set), shows them to the model, and prints the answer plus Sources: [[...]]. Only citations that resolve to real pages are kept; an invented link becomes plain text. With no valid citation it prints I find nothing about this in the wiki. (in the notes' language) rather than an ungrounded answer (exit 0).

It also checks the sentences. Each sentence with facts in it must find its numbers, proper names and most of its key words in the pages the model was given or cited (accents, case, plurals and endings ignored; no model call). A sentence that fails gets a ⚠ after it, and one line at the end lists what was not found (Not found in the cited pages: Nobel, 1902; No encontrado en las páginas citadas: ... in Spanish). When most of the sentences fail, the answer is refused like an uncited one. A sentence that says the pages do not have the answer is not checked, and neither is an answer whose pages are all in another language than the notes. It is a vocabulary check, not a meaning check. [run].check_answers = false turns it off. Details and measurements: Ask your wiki.

Option Default Meaning --json off Print one JSON object (answer, cited, refused, saved, unsupported) instead of the text. A refused answer is a normal object with refused: true and exit 0. See JSON output --save off File a grounded answer (with its ⚠ marks and footer, if it has any) as wiki/syntheses/<question>.md, update index.md and log.md, and commit. The page is named after your question (cut at about 80 characters); a name that already belongs to another page gets (synthesis) ((síntesis) in Spanish) 
sb ask "What is the forgetting curve and how does it relate to notes?"

The forgetting curve describes the rate at which learned material is forgotten unless reviewed [[Forgetting Curve]]. It suggests that most learned material is forgotten within days unless reviewed.

Sources: [[Spaced Repetition]], [[Forgetting Curve]]

For a concept or entity page the model reads the page's consolidated ## Summary first, then its other sections, within the same size budget. It uses [llm.ask] if set, otherwise [llm.summarize]; with run.rewrite_questions = true it first asks the model for search words in the notes' language and English. Every question is appended to .esbi/asks.jsonl (the pages retrieved and cited, how many sentences were marked unsupported, tokens, seconds). A model error prints error: ... and exits 1.

docs.title: sb eval
docs.text:
sb eval [--config PATH] [--k 6] [--rewrite] [--answers]

Scores retrieval, the step where sb ask picks the pages the model will read, on questions whose source you know. The questions live in <vault>/.esbi/golden.jsonl, one JSON object per line, with the start of the expected title(s):

{"question": "What is an agent harness?", "expect": ["Code as Agent Harness"]}
Option Default Meaning --k N 6 How many pages count as retrieved (sb ask uses 6) --rewrite off First rewrite each question into search terms (one call each, with the ask model) --answers off Also run sb ask on each question and report how many answers were grounded and cite the expected page (slow)

With no flag it needs no model and finishes in about a second. Without the file it explains the format and exits 1. See Ask your wiki.

Retrieval on 4 questions: recall@6 75% (3/4), MRR 0.44
  miss: How do I cook rice? (expected Arroz; got nothing)

docs.title: sb bench
docs.text:
sb bench [--config PATH] [--models a,b,c] [--cases N]

Runs the same ingest and ask cases, built from your own vault (raw snapshots and concept pages), through each model, and prints a comparison: success rate, share needing no retry, median latency, tokens per case, estimated cost, the share written in the right language ([notes].language), concepts per source, and whether answers cite the right page. It ends with a routing suggestion and saves the report in .esbi/bench/. It reads the wiki but never writes to it and never changes config.toml.

Option Default Meaning --models a,b,c [bench].models Comma-separated provider/model list --cases N [bench].cases (3) Cases per task

A model is suggested only if it succeeds on at least 80% of its cases. Without models, or with an empty vault, it exits 1 (error: pass --models or set [bench].models in config.toml; error: the vault has no sources or concepts to test with yet). See Choose how the notes are written.

docs.title: sb export
docs.text:
sb export [--out DIR] [--config PATH]

Writes the wiki as plain HTML files: a front page listing sources, concepts, entities and syntheses, one page per note, [[links]] turned into links, figures copied. raw/ is never exported.

Option Default Meaning --out DIR <vault>/site Where to write the site

Running it again replaces the previous export. It refuses to write into a folder that has other files in it and is not an export (error: ... is not an export of this wiki and has other files: not touching it, exit 1), so it can never wipe something else. The page loads Mermaid from a CDN, so diagrams need an internet connection; everything else works offline. See Export a website.

Exported 11 pages. Open ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/site/index.html

docs.title: sb ocr status
docs.text:
sb ocr status [--config PATH]

Says whether reading images and scanned PDFs is on, which model it uses, whether Ollama has it, its download size, this machine's memory, and whether Ollama is new enough for it. It changes nothing and asks no model.

Reading images and scanned PDFs: on.
Model: ollama/qwen3-vl:2b-instruct
The model is installed in Ollama.
Download size: 1.9 GB.
Machine memory: 8 GB.
This model is best with 8 GB or more: this machine can likely run it.
Ollama: 0.13.5 (the model needs 0.12.7 or later).

Without an [llm.ocr] section it says off (never set up) and prints the recommended model. With enabled = false it says off and that the model choice is kept. If Ollama cannot be reached it says so instead of guessing.

docs.title: sb ocr enable
docs.text:
sb ocr enable [--model NAME] [--pull] [--config PATH]

Turns reading images and scanned PDFs on by writing the [llm.ocr] section of the config (adding it, or setting enabled = true and the model; the rest of the file is not touched), then says whether Ollama has the model.

Option Default Meaning --model NAME the model already in the config, else the recommended qwen3-vl:2b-instruct Which Ollama vision model to use. Only an Ollama model on this machine works --pull off Download the model now if Ollama does not have it. Without it, at a keyboard it asks Download it now? (default No); in a script it only prints the ollama pull command

It warns, and never blocks, when this machine has less memory than the model wants or Ollama is older than the model needs. deepseek-ocr:3b is a known choice for a machine with 16 GB of memory or more; it is never the default.

Reading images and scanned PDFs is on, with qwen3-vl:2b-instruct. Changed: [llm.ocr] in ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml
qwen3-vl:2b-instruct is installed.

docs.title: sb ocr disable
docs.text:
sb ocr disable [--config PATH]

Turns it off by setting enabled = false in [llm.ocr]; the model choice stays, so sb ocr enable brings it back without typing. Images in inbox/ are then listed by sb scan as not read, and scanned PDFs are rejected. When it is already off it says so and changes nothing.

docs.title: sb setup email
docs.text:
sb setup email [--config PATH]

A guided wizard (bash, bundled with the app) that connects a Gmail mailbox in six stages: turn on 2-Step Verification, create the esbi-cli label, route you+esbi-cli@gmail.com into it, create an app password, save the settings and the password (the password goes straight into the Keychain), and test it. Stop with Ctrl-C and run it again: nothing changes until stage 5. The full guide is Capture email.

docs.title: sb setup clipper
docs.text:
sb setup clipper [--config PATH]

A guided wizard in five stages: install the Obsidian Web Clipper extension, point it at your vault, import the two templates, clip a test page, and let the worker pick it up. It needs Obsidian: with viewer = "none" it explains that and exits 0. See Web Clipper and YouTube.

docs.title: sb email fetch
docs.text:
sb email fetch [--config PATH]

Saves mail from the configured Gmail label as clip notes (and PDF and image attachments) in inbox/, skipping mail already saved (by Message-ID). It takes every unread mail in the label however old, every mail added to the label after the highest UID it has taken (remembered per mailbox generation in .esbi/mail-state.json), and every mail of the last 14 days counted from the day it was received: see Which mail is taken. It marks a mail as seen only after its note is written and never deletes mail. sb run does this for you.

Mail: 2 saved, 0 duplicates, 0 failed, 1 images saved, 3 links queued.

The last counts appear only when they are not zero, and there is one more, N not marked as read (the server refused), for mail that was saved but whose read flag the server would not set. images saved counts PNG, JPEG, WEBP and TIFF attachments kept in inbox/ (the bytes decide what a file is; pictures under 200 px or a few KB, such as signatures and tracking pixels, over 5 MB, or beyond 15 MB per mail are skipped); they are read later with the local [llm.ocr] model when it is on. links queued counts the links put in the queue when [email].follow_links is on: they are not fetched here (see Links in a mail). Both count as email for the privacy rules.

Needs [email].enabled = true and [email].user; otherwise error: email is disabled: set [email].enabled = true in config.toml (exit 1). A login or label error is printed with its cause and exits 1.

docs.title: sb email configure
docs.text:
sb email configure --user ADDRESS [--label NAME] [--config PATH]

Turns on mail capture in config.toml without the wizard: replaces the [email] block (or adds it) and touches nothing else. The password is stored separately with sb email set-password.

Option Default Meaning --user ADDRESS required The Gmail address that receives your forwards --label NAME esbi-cli The Gmail label to read 
Mail capture on for you@gmail.com, label esbi-cli, in ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml

docs.title: sb email set-password
docs.text:
sb email set-password [--stdin] [--config PATH]

Prompts (hidden) for the mailbox app password and stores it in the macOS Keychain, service esbi-cli-imap (off macOS, which is not supported, in the system keyring through a Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet; where there is none, it says there is no keyring and where email capture works: see Email where there is no keyring). Spaces in a Gmail-style password are dropped. It needs [email].user in the config first. There is deliberately no --password VALUE option: a value on the command line is kept in your shell history and visible in the process list.

Option Meaning --stdin Read the password from standard input, to paste without typing: pbpaste \| sb email set-password --stdin. Clear the clipboard afterwards 
App password for you@gmail.com:
Saved to the Keychain.

(Saved to the system keyring. off macOS.)

docs.title: sb schedule install
docs.text:
sb schedule install [--config PATH] [--agents-dir DIR]

Writes and loads the launchd agent com.esbi-cli.nightly that runs sb run --if-due at [run].nightly_time, at login, and hourly as a retry net (macOS only). It uses the environment that is running sb, so it works wherever that lives, and the config is resolved to an absolute path. Run it again after changing nightly_time, and after moving or reinstalling sb.

Option Default Meaning --agents-dir DIR ~/Library/LaunchAgents Where launchd agents live 
Installed ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.esbi-cli.nightly.plist
Runs every day at 03:00 (or at the next wake). Log: ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/.esbi/logs/nightly.log

The first run needs a macOS permission: see Run it every night. On a system without launchd (not macOS, so not supported), the command stops with exit code 1, writes nothing and prints the cron line that does the same, the one sb init --nightly prints:

error: the nightly job uses launchd, which only macOS has. On this system add this line to cron (`crontab -e`; every hour: the first tick after [run].nightly_time runs the nightly batch, later ones drain what is queued, up to [run].max_batches_per_day batches a day):
  0 * * * * /home/you/.local/bin/sb run --if-due --config /home/you/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml

The line names sb by its absolute path (cron's PATH is /usr/bin:/bin, so a bare sb installed in ~/.local/bin would never be found), quotes a path with spaces and writes a % as \%.

See cron on other systems.

docs.title: sb schedule status
docs.text:
sb schedule status [--agents-dir DIR]

Prints whether the agent file exists (installed:) and whether launchd has it loaded (loaded:). Without launchd there is nothing to query, so it prints the same cron advice as sb schedule install and exits 0.

installed: yes
loaded: yes

docs.title: sb schedule uninstall
docs.text:
sb schedule uninstall [--agents-dir DIR]

Unloads the agent and deletes its file. It also removes a job installed under the old project name. Prints Removed. or Nothing to remove. Without launchd it prints the same cron advice and exits 1: remove your cron line with crontab -e.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: All settings live in one TOML file, config.toml. sb init writes a first version; this page lists every key, its default, and a complete example for the common setups. For the choice between models, read Choose how the notes are written first.

docs.title: Where the config file is
docs.text:
The first file that exists in this list is used:

  1. --config PATH, given to the command.
  2. The ESBI_CONFIG environment variable.
  3. ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml (where sb init writes it).
  4. A config.toml next to an editable install of the project (so a uv tool install --editable copy works from any folder).

A config.toml in the current folder is never read: a cloned repository could otherwise point the model or the mailbox at someone else's server.

sb info prints which file is used. A file you name on purpose must exist: if the --config path (or the file ESBI_CONFIG points at) is missing, the command stops with error: config file not found: PATH and exit code 1. Only the default places (3 and 4) are tried one after the other without a message.

sb info

config=~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml
vault=~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi
viewer=none
language=en
email=disabled

Edit the file with any editor. There is nothing to reload: the next command reads it again. Two things need a second step: a changed nightly_time needs sb schedule install again, and a changed [llm.embed] model rebuilds the page index on the next sb ask or sb run.

The file is checked whenever it is read, in every section. A misspelled key, an unknown section, or a value of the wrong type stops the command with one error: line (exit code 1) that names the section, the key and what is valid, and sb doctor shows it as FAIL config:

error: [llm.summarize] has an unknown key 'num_ctxx' (did you mean 'num_ctx'?). Valid keys: model, base_url, api_key_env, num_ctx, temperature, timeout_seconds, fallback, max_tokens
error: [run].max_chunks must be a whole number, got 'ten'

docs.title: A complete file
docs.text:
This is the starter file (config.example.toml) with every key at its default. Lines starting with # are optional sections.

[paths]
vault = "~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi"
# legacy_vault = "~/Notes/old-links"

[notes]
language = "en"
viewer = "obsidian"

[run]
max_source_chars = 4000
chunk_chars = 8000
max_chunks = 16
max_calls_per_source = 60
ocr_max_pages = 10
find_connections = true
rewrite_questions = false
check_answers = true
nightly_time = "03:00"
max_sources_per_run = 20
max_batches_per_day = 6
max_consolidations_per_run = 0
max_tokens_per_run = 300000
# max_usd_per_run = 2.0
flag_contradictions = false

[llm.summarize]
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
num_ctx = 8192

# [llm.synthesize]
# [llm.private]
# [llm.ocr]
# [llm.ask]
# [llm.embed]

[bench]
models = ["ollama/llama3.2:latest"]
cases = 3

[bench.prices]

# [update]
# check = true

# [network]
# use_environment_proxy = false

[email]
enabled = false
imap_host = "imap.gmail.com"
mailbox = "esbi-cli"
# user = "you@gmail.com"
# follow_links = true
# follow_links_max = 3

docs.title: [paths]
docs.text: Key Default Meaning vault required The vault folder. ~ is expanded. Without it every command fails with config.toml needs [paths].vault. The folder must exist: if it does not (a typo, an unmounted drive), every command that opens the vault stops with error: vault not found: PATH (--json code vault_not_found) and creates nothing. sb init makes it, and sb doctor, sb init and the commands that only edit the config (sb ocr ..., sb email set-password) work without it legacy_vault none An older folder with Links/ and PDFs/, read only by sb import-legacy

docs.title: [notes]
docs.text: Key Default Meaning language "en" The language the notes are written in: "en" (English) or "es" (Spanish). It sets the instruction to the model, the section headings (Executive summary, Resumen ejecutivo...), the daily index, index.md, the lint and benchmark reports and the answers and refusals of sb ask. Quotes stay in the source's language. Any other value is an error that lists the supported ones. A missing key means "en". See Language of the notes viewer "obsidian" "obsidian" opens notes with obsidian:// links; "none" makes sb today print a path and stops sb doctor asking you to open the folder in Obsidian. Anything else is an error

docs.title: Language of the notes
docs.text:
[notes].language is the one setting that decides the language of everything the program writes into the wiki. The command line itself (messages, --help, errors) is always English.

Value Language Example heading "en" English (the default) ## Executive summary "es" Spanish ## Resumen ejecutivo

What follows the setting: the notes' section headings and labels (## From [[Source]] on concept pages), the daily index and the Home.md block, index.md, the lint report, the sb bench report, and what sb ask answers and refuses with. The instruction to the model says which language to write in; if the model answers in the wrong language, the worker asks once more and then keeps the answer with a warning.

Changing the setting is safe: the worker never rewrites a note by itself. Notes already written keep their language, and every reader (privacy filters, sb ask, read ticks, sb reingest) recognises the headings of both languages, so a vault can hold both. To rebuild the old notes in the new language, run sb reingest --all (see Manage the queue). Your SCHEMA.md is never overwritten; its Language paragraph says which language the notes are in, and the setting wins if they disagree.

sb init --language en|es writes the setting and the vault's SCHEMA.md and index.md in that language. To add a language, see Add a language.

docs.title: [run]
docs.text: Key Default Meaning max_source_chars 4000 A source up to this many characters is read by the model in one go; a longer one is read in chunks (see How a note is made) chunk_chars 8000 Size of each chunk of a long source max_chunks 16 How many notes the plan and the summary are written from. A source with more chunks than this is read in full: every chunk gets its notes, then the notes are merged into sections of 5 (level by level) until at most max_chunks remain. Sampling is gone. A source with at most this many chunks is read exactly as before. See Long sources max_calls_per_source 60 A hard cap on the model calls for one source, retries included; at least 12 (a smaller value is an error when the config is read). Calls are kept back for merging what was read and for the plan, the summary and the connections, so when the cap stops the reading early the note says which part was not read (a warning callout at the top, and a warning in the run). A source of 40 chunks takes about 55 calls; raise it for books (a source needing more than about 45 chunks is read only as far as the cap allows) ocr_max_pages 10 A scanned PDF is read (OCR) up to this many pages; the run says when it stopped short find_connections true One extra model call per source that relates the new note to pages you already have, with the reason. false skips it (faster, no "Connections to your wiki" section) rewrite_questions false sb ask first asks the model for search words in the notes' language and in English (one small extra call). Finds notes whose words differ from the question's. Measured on 16 questions: right page in the top 6 for 88% without, 94% with check_answers true sb ask checks each sentence of an answer against the pages the model was given and cited: a ⚠ after a sentence whose numbers, proper names or key words are not in them, a footer naming what was not found, and a refusal when most sentences fail. No model call. It compares vocabulary, not meaning, and was measured only on Spanish with llama3.2; set false to switch it off (for another language or model you do not trust it with, or to see the unchecked answer). See Ask your wiki nightly_time "03:00" When the nightly job runs, HH:MM in 24 hours. Re-run sb schedule install after changing it. A bad value is rejected when the config is read max_sources_per_run 20 Sources per run (sb run --limit overrides it) max_batches_per_day 6 How many scheduled batches the job runs in a day: a whole number of at least 1 (anything else is an error when the config is read). It counts the scheduled runs (sb run --if-due) since the last nightly_time, the nightly run included, so with the defaults the night's run and up to five hourly batches drain the queue and then stop until the next night. The hourly tick runs the next batch whenever sources are queued, whatever ended the last one (max_sources_per_run, max_tokens_per_run, max_usd_per_run, or an empty queue that filled again), so this cap is what bounds a day's work and spend. A run that stopped for a model outage or an interruption does not count, and neither does a manual sb run. Before this key, a large backlog was drained one batch per hour all day with no limit. See Run it every night max_consolidations_per_run 0 How many concept and entity pages one run may give a consolidated ## Summary by itself (after the sources, for the pages it just wrote that reached three sources, or two more than at their last summary). 0 is off, and that is the default on purpose: a 3B model such as llama3.2 writes summaries that read well but sometimes state relations the sections do not say, so read a few first with sb consolidate (manual, never capped) and turn this on (for example 5) together with a stronger [llm.synthesize] model. See Consolidated summaries max_tokens_per_run 300000 A run stops once the models have used this many tokens; what is left stays queued max_usd_per_run unset (no cap) A number of USD, more than 0 (0 or a negative value is an error when the config is read). A run stops once its estimated cost reaches it; what is left stays queued, with no attempt counted, and the run is recorded as usd_budget (also the stopped_by of sb run --json). The estimate is the tokens each model used times its price in [bench.prices] (USD per million tokens, the table sb bench uses). Only models that send text out count: a model on this machine costs 0, and so do claude-cli/ and codex-cli/, which are flat-rate subscriptions. A model with no price counts as 0, so with no [bench.prices] entry the cap never stops anything. With a fallback its tokens are priced at the dearer of the two models. The check happens between sources, so the source being read when the cap is reached finishes first flag_contradictions false When true, the model may flag contradictions between a new source and existing pages: they become notes in wiki/review/ and a [!warning] on the page. Off because small models flag tenuous ones; turn it on with a stronger model

docs.title: [llm.<task>]
docs.text:
One section per task. Each task can use a different model.

Section Used for If absent [llm.summarize] Required. Takes notes on each chunk of a long source; writes the whole note when there is no synthesize Every command that needs a model fails, saying there is no [llm.summarize] section [llm.synthesize] Writes the core note, the abstract and the connections (a few calls per source). Use a stronger model here: reading is cheap, synthesis is where quality is made summarize does it [llm.ask] sb ask, question rewriting, sb eval --rewrite/--answers summarize [llm.private] The only model that reads email. Must run on this machine Emails are refused while a cloud model is set [llm.ocr] Reads images and scanned PDFs. Must be an Ollama vision model on this machine. Optional: sb ocr enable and sb ocr disable write it for you Images are not read; scanned PDFs are rejected [llm.embed] Embeddings for search by meaning (hybrid search). Only ollama/<model> Search is by keyword only

Any [llm.<task>] section accepts these keys:

Key Default Meaning model required <provider>/<name>, see the providers below base_url the provider's usual address Where the server is. For Ollama and LM Studio, an address that is not this machine is reported by sb doctor as sending text out, and email is kept off it api_key_env OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY The name of the environment variable that holds the key. Keys are never written in the file num_ctx 8192 The context window, in tokens. Ollama only temperature 0.2 Sampling temperature. Not used by claude-cli or codex-cli timeout_seconds 300 Seconds to wait for one answer. A timeout fails that chunk or source; the run goes on. The old name timeout is a deprecated alias: it still works, and timeout_seconds wins when both are set. The one-line notice (notice: [llm.summarize] timeout is now timeout_seconds, on stderr) is printed once a day per config file, not on every command (the time is kept in notices.json in the cache folder, ~/.cache/esbi-cli or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/esbi-cli; if that folder cannot be written you only get the notice more often). sb doctor always prints it max_tokens none A cap on the length of an answer. Ollama only. Set it on the model that reads chunks: small models sometimes loop on one input, and the cap turns a 5-minute timeout into seconds enabled true Only in [llm.ocr] (any other section rejects it as an unknown key). false switches reading images and scanned PDFs off and keeps the model choice, so turning it back on needs no typing: sb ocr disable and sb ocr enable do the same from the command line fallback none A second <provider>/<name> used when the main model cannot be reached (a spent usage window, a lost login, a server down). A timeout does not trigger it. sb doctor checks it too

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
Provider Talks to Notes ollama/<name> Ollama's API, default http://localhost:11434 Nothing leaves your machine unless base_url points elsewhere or the name ends in -cloud lmstudio/<identifier> LM Studio's local server, default http://localhost:1234/v1 No key. The identifier is what lms ls shows openai/<name> Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint Set base_url for OpenRouter and similar. Key from OPENAI_API_KEY or api_key_env. Text goes to that provider anthropic/<name> Anthropic's Messages API Key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or api_key_env. Text goes to Anthropic claude-cli/<model> The official claude command, paid by your Claude Pro or Max subscription claude-cli/default (your account's model) or claude-cli/sonnet. No key in any file; log in once with claude auth login. max_tokens and num_ctx do not apply codex-cli/<model> The official codex command, paid by your ChatGPT plan codex-cli/default (the model your Codex is set to) or a model name Codex knows. No key in any file; log in once with codex login. A fallback works as with the other providers. max_tokens, num_ctx and temperature do not apply. See Using a ChatGPT plan

A model that sends text away (openai, anthropic, claude-cli, codex-cli, and a remote Ollama or LM Studio) is never shown email. The rules are in Safety and privacy.

docs.title: Using a subscription
docs.text: Log in once with claude auth login (Claude Code must be installed), then point a task at it. Three things to know. (1) Every call counts against your plan's usage windows (a session limit and a weekly one). When you hit one, the call fails with the tool's message, the run stops like any other model outage, nothing is lost, and the next run resumes. (2) The tool is started with its tools, settings, plugins and MCP servers switched off: otherwise one call carried about 450,000 tokens of your own setup (about 700 with them off). (3) How Anthropic counts non-interactive use against a plan has changed before; check your plan's terms.

docs.title: Using a ChatGPT plan
docs.text:
Install OpenAI's codex tool, log in once with codex login, then point a task at codex-cli/default (or codex-cli/<model>). sb doctor checks that codex is installed and logged in. Four things to know. (1) Every call counts against your plan's usage windows; when you hit one the call fails with the tool's message, the run stops like any other model outage, nothing is lost, and the next run resumes (a local fallback keeps it going meanwhile). (2) The call runs read-only, in an empty scratch folder, with the tool's own tools, rules and your Codex settings switched off: the model gets the prompt and nothing else of yours. (3) The text of each source goes to OpenAI, so the worker treats it like any model that sends text out: email is never shown to it (keep a local [llm.private]). (4) It was measured once, against codex-cli 0.146.0 on a ChatGPT plan: the strict schema the worker sends was accepted, a call takes 9 to 12 seconds, and every call carries about 8,500 tokens of the tool's own overhead. That suits the nightly run, a few calls per source; it is a poor fit for a model that makes many small calls, so keep the reading model ([llm.summarize]) local and put only the writing one ([llm.synthesize]) here. It has not been exercised more widely than that.

[llm.synthesize]
model = "codex-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 600

docs.title: [email]
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning enabled false Fetch mail during sb run imap_host "imap.gmail.com" The IMAP server mailbox "esbi-cli" The mailbox name to read; for Gmail, the label user none The mailbox address. The app password is not here: it lives in the macOS Keychain under the service esbi-cli-imap (off macOS, which is not supported, the system keyring: see Email where there is no keyring) follow_links false Queue the http(s) links found in the text of a mail, so the pages they lead to become notes too. See Links in a mail follow_links_max 3 At most this many links are queued per mail, from 1 to 10 (anything else is an error when the config is read)

sb setup email or sb email configure writes this block for you, and keeps follow_links and follow_links_max if they were already there.

docs.title: Links in a mail
docs.text:
With follow_links = true, the links in the text of each newly saved mail are queued, never fetched while the mail is captured. The nightly run then reads them like any queued source, with its limits, and treats what it finds as email: only [llm.private] (a model on this machine) writes the note, the note has kind: email, and a cloud model is never shown it, exactly like the mail it came from. Tracking redirects, unsubscribe, preferences, view-in-browser and account-action links (sign in, confirm, reset password, activate...), and pictures, are skipped; a link already queued or already a note is not queued again.
