Only links that show as text in the mail are found: a link hidden behind a button or anchor text in an HTML-only mail is not.

It is off by default because opening a link is a visit: the site that sent the mail, or whoever put the link there, sees a request from your machine (through your IP address, and at the time the nightly run reaches it). Fetching still goes through the same public-address guard as any link (see Safety and privacy). Turn it on only for mail you trust to link to pages you would open anyway.

The queue shows these as ordinary sources; the capture line says how many: Mail: 3 saved, 0 duplicates, 0 failed, 2 images saved, 5 links queued.

docs.title: [network]
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning use_environment_proxy false Fetching a link (and the update check) ignores HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and NO_PROXY. true honours them, for a network whose only way out is a proxy

Why off: the check that a link points at a public address describes where the request goes only when this machine connects itself. Behind a proxy it is the proxy that resolves the name and connects, so the check no longer says where the request ended up, and a proxy inside your network can be made to reach internal hosts through a link in an email. With the setting on, the address checks are the proxy's, not esbi-cli's, and sb doctor shows WARN network for as long as it is set. Nothing but this setting turns the proxy on: it is read from the config of the command that is running, and every command starts with it off.

docs.title: [bench]
docs.text:
Used by sb bench, and prices is also the price list for [run].max_usd_per_run; nothing here changes which model the worker uses.

Key Default Meaning models none The candidate models, ["ollama/qwen3:4b", ...] cases 3 Cases per task prices none The [bench.prices] table: USD per million tokens (input and output blended) per model, for the cost estimate. Local models cost 0. It is also what [run].max_usd_per_run multiplies a run's tokens by 
[bench.prices]
"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5" = 9.0

docs.title: [update]
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning check true Once a day, ask GitHub whether a newer release exists, and print one line after a command run in a terminal when there is one. false turns the check off. sb update and sb version --check always ask, because you asked them to

What is sent: one anonymous HTTPS GET to api.github.com (the releases API), whose request carries a User-Agent naming esbi-cli and its version. No vault data, no identifier, nothing from the config. Nothing is installed by itself. The nightly job (sb run) never checks. See Update esbi-cli.

The setting is read from the config sb finds without --config (the default places, or ESBI_CONFIG). To be sure the check is off whatever the config, set ESBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Used for ESBI_CONFIG The config file, when --config is not given ESBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK 1 turns off the automatic update check, whatever [update].check says ANTHROPIC_API_KEY The key for anthropic/... models (or the variable named by api_key_env) OPENAI_API_KEY The key for openai/... models (or the variable named by api_key_env) HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY Ignored when fetching web pages, unless [network] use_environment_proxy = true; see [network] UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT Only for development from a checkout: keeps the virtual environment out of an iCloud-synced folder

docs.title: Setups
docs.text: Each block is the whole [llm.*] part of the file for that setup. Everything else stays as it is.

docs.title: All local (Ollama)
docs.text:
[llm.summarize]
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 300
num_ctx = 8192
max_tokens = 1200

This is what sb init --model local writes. Nothing leaves your machine. Needs ollama pull llama3.2.

docs.title: All local (LM Studio)
docs.text:
[llm.summarize]
model = "lmstudio/qwen2.5-7b-instruct"
timeout_seconds = 300

Use the identifier lms ls shows. sb init --model local --runtime lmstudio --local-model NAME writes it. Add base_url = "http://localhost:1234/v1" only if the server runs on another port.

docs.title: Subscription, with a local fallback
docs.text:
[llm.summarize]
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 300

[llm.synthesize]
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 600

[llm.ask]
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 600

[llm.private]
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

This is what sb init --model subscription writes. A good split is a local reading model (many small calls) and only the writing model on the subscription (a few calls per source): a 3-chunk source took about one minute that way, against several locally.

docs.title: API key
docs.text:
[llm.summarize]
model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 300

[llm.ask]
model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
timeout_seconds = 600

[llm.private]
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

Set the key in the environment (export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... in your shell profile; for the nightly job the variable must be visible to launchd, which does not read your shell profile, so prefer the subscription or a local model for unattended runs). For an OpenAI-compatible service use model = "openai/gpt-4o-mini", and base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1" with api_key_env = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY" for OpenRouter.

docs.title: Ollama on another machine
docs.text:
[llm.summarize]
model = "ollama/qwen3:8b"
base_url = "http://192.168.1.50:11434"
timeout_seconds = 900

The notes' text goes to that machine, so email is kept off it (and [llm.private] must stay on this one). sb init --base-url writes the same and warns; sb doctor keeps a WARN server summarize line.

docs.title: Different models for different jobs
docs.text:
[llm.summarize]            # reads each chunk: many cheap calls
model = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"
max_tokens = 1200

[llm.synthesize]           # writes the note: a few calls
model = "claude-cli/default"
fallback = "ollama/llama3.2:latest"

[llm.ask]
model = "ollama/qwen3:4b"

docs.title: Images and scanned PDFs (OCR)
docs.text:
[llm.ocr]
model = "ollama/qwen3-vl:2b-instruct"
timeout_seconds = 600

sb init --ocr or sb ocr enable writes it (and sb ocr enable --pull downloads the model). Run ollama pull qwen3-vl:2b-instruct once (1.9 GB). The model must run on this machine; another provider, another host, a -cloud model or a fallback is refused. To stop reading images without losing the model choice, set enabled = false in the same section (or run sb ocr disable):

[llm.ocr]
model = "ollama/qwen3-vl:2b-instruct"
enabled = false

qwen3-vl:2b-instruct is the recommended model and fits an 8 GB Mac. deepseek-ocr:3b (6.7 GB) is a choice for a machine with 16 GB of memory or more; on 8 GB it was measured unusable (about 100 times slower). See Choosing the OCR model.

docs.title: Search by meaning (embeddings)
docs.text:
[llm.embed]
model = "ollama/nomic-embed-text"
timeout_seconds = 60

Run ollama pull nomic-embed-text once (about 270 MB). Pages are embedded once, by section, in .esbi/index.sqlite3, and again only when they change. With the section absent, or the embedder unreachable, search is exactly the keyword search. Email is never sent to an embedder that is not on this machine. Details and measurements: Hybrid retrieval.

docs.title: Without Obsidian
docs.text:
[notes]
viewer = "none"

See Use it without Obsidian.

docs.title: The daily index
docs.text:
Home.md links to today's note, wiki/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md. It is regenerated from the vault's state every run, so your ticks are never lost.

The headings follow [notes].language; the table gives the English heading, and the Spanish one in brackets.

Section Content Read (Leído) Sources the worker saw you tick since the last index Processed today (Procesado hoy) Every source processed today, as a checkbox with its one-line summary. Tick it when you have read it Tomorrow's queue (Cola de mañana) How many sources are still queued, and the oldest 20 (by clip title or file name when known, else the URL) To review (Por revisar) When the latest run could not reach the model, a first line says so with the time and how many sources are waiting (The model server was unreachable in the last run (...): 3 sources are waiting. Start Ollama or check the model, then runsb run.); it disappears after a run that reached the model. Then review notes (contradictions, Lint.md, summaries that failed their checks, possible merges of pages), sources that failed for good, and sources being retried with their attempt number and last error Revisit (Repasar) Three older notes, rotating daily Runs (Ejecuciones) Today's runs: time, counts, tokens, duration, why it stopped Statistics (Estadísticas) Page counts, today's activity, read progress, orphan pages

Every file in wiki/review/ is listed under To review, so the notes the consolidated summaries add show up there too: <page> - summary to review (resumen por revisar) and <page> - possible merge (posible fusión). They are described in What lives where. An interrupted nightly run does not count as that day's run, so its Runs line ends with stopped: interrupted (the other reasons are source limit, token budget, USD budget and model unavailable) and the job tries again.

Ticking works both ways: a ticked source becomes status: read, and unticking its box puts it back to processed (its read date is cleared). The undo only looks at the box in the daily note of the day the source was processed: that note is regenerated from state, so a read source always shows ticked there and an unticked box can only be your doing. A source with no box in that note, or ticked anywhere in it, is left as it is; unticking in any other day's note changes nothing. It happens the next time sb index or sb run registers ticks (Put 1 source back to unread.).

The routine, step by step: Read your notes and tick what you have read. A tick is only read from a line shaped - [x] [[Source title]]. Home.md links to today's note; between its <!-- esbi:start --> and <!-- esbi:end --> comments it shows today's link, how many sources are unread, and how many are queued, and the worker rewrites only that block.

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text: For a program that runs sb (an editor plugin, a script), seven commands print JSON instead of text when given --json: sb version, status, info, doctor, add, ask and run. This page is the contract: what is printed, what will not change under you, and how a failure looks. Reading output for people? The command reference describes the text.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
• One object per line, on stdout, and nothing else. Every command prints exactly one line of JSON, except sb run, which prints one line per event (JSON Lines, below). The output is ASCII (non-ASCII characters are \uXXXX escapes), and each line is flushed as soon as it is written, so a reader sees sb run progress as it happens.
  • Human text goes to stderr. A warning (warning: git commit failed), the update notice and the Interrupted: line are on stderr and never on stdout. A reader that parses stdout needs no other filter.
  • Exit codes do not change. They are the same as without --json: 0 success, 1 an error, 130 and 143 after Ctrl-C and SIGTERM (see Stopping a command). sb doctor --json exits 1 when a check is FAIL, and still prints its object.
  • Every object carries "contract", the contract number (see below).
  • No traceback. A failure is an error object (below) with exit 1, not Python's stack trace.
sb status --json

{"contract": 1, "vault": "/Users/you/Documents/Obsidian/esbi", "queue": {"queued": 2, "processing": 0, "done": 5, "failed": 1}, "failed": [{"target": "https://example.com/", "attempts": 3, "error": "ExtractError: No readable article content found at https://example.com/"}], "retrying": []}

docs.title: The contract number
docs.text:
contract is 1. A program should read it, and read it first: the way to ask which contract an installed sb speaks, and which version it is, is

sb version --json

{"contract": 1, "version": "0.3.0"}

The rule for changes:

  • Additive changes keep the number. A new field in an object, a new command with --json, a new event name in sb run, a new value of stopped_by, a new error code: contract stays 1. So a reader must ignore fields, events and codes it does not know, and never fail on them.
  • A breaking change bumps the number. Removing or renaming a field, changing its type or meaning, or changing the shape of an object, makes contract 2. A reader that sees a number it does not know should stop and say that this sb is newer than the reader.

sb version --json is available from the first release that has --json; a reader that gets no such option: --json from it is talking to an older sb that has no contract at all.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A failure is one object and exit 1:

{"contract": 1, "error": "config file not found: /tmp/typo.toml", "code": "config_not_found"}

error is a one-line message for a person (its wording may change); code is for the program and will not change under contract 1.

code Means Raised by config_not_found No config file: a --config path (or ESBI_CONFIG) that does not exist, or none in the default places every command that reads the config bad_config The config is invalid (a misspelled key, a wrong type, an unknown provider in model), or a model cannot be built from it status, info, add, ask, run vault_not_found [paths].vault points at a folder that does not exist (a typo, an unmounted drive). Nothing is created. sb doctor and the commands that only edit the config do not raise it every command that opens the vault bad_target An argument of sb add is not an http(s) URL or an existing .pdf, .md or (with OCR on) image file. Nothing was queued add os_error A file or disk problem: a read-only or full vault, a missing permission, a vault's state database that cannot be used, or no home folder. error is the one line a person would read (Permission denied: /path) every command that touches files llm_error The model could not be reached or failed while answering ask run_in_progress Another run holds the lock. Exit 0, as without --json: skipping is not a failure run

A new code can appear later (additive): treat an unknown code as a generic failure.

docs.title: sb version
docs.text:
sb version --json prints {"contract": 1, "version": "0.3.0"}. --check is not honoured: it prints no network answer.

Field Type Meaning contract number The contract number version text The installed version, as sb version prints it

docs.title: sb status
docs.text: Field Type Meaning vault text Absolute path of the vault queue object queued, processing, done, failed: how many sources are in each state (numbers, 0 when none). A source still being retried counts as queued failed list The sources parked after their last attempt: {"target", "attempts", "error"} (text, number, text) retrying list The queued sources that have failed before: {"target", "attempts", "error"}

docs.title: sb info
docs.text: Field Type Meaning version text The installed version config text Absolute path of the config file in use vault text Absolute path of the vault viewer text obsidian or none language text The notes' language code (en, es) models object The model per task that is configured, as provider/name text: summarize, and each of synthesize, private, ocr, embed that is set. ask is always there: it is the [llm.ask] model, else the summarize one sends_text_out object For each task in models (same keys), true when the text of a source leaves this machine for that model (an API, claude-cli, codex-cli, a remote Ollama or LM Studio server, an Ollama -cloud model) and false when it stays (Ollama or LM Studio on this machine). A model that cannot be built from the config counts as true: a client uses this to warn, so the doubtful case errs on the safe side. It is the same rule that keeps email away from a model: a client can show it instead of guessing from the provider name. Added in 0.3.0 without changing contract (1) nightly object installed (true or false: the launchd job is loaded; false where there is no launchd) and time (text, HH:MM, from [run].nightly_time)

docs.title: sb doctor
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning ok true or false true when no check is FAIL (warnings do not count). The exit code is 1 when this is false checks list One entry per line of the text output, in the same order

Each check is {"level", "name", "text", "fix"}, all text: level is ok, WARN or FAIL; name is the label of the text output (config, version, vault, model summarize, ocr, ocr memory, network...); text the message; fix what to do, or the empty text when there is nothing to fix. A broken config is still an object, with a FAIL config check, not an error object. The checks are listed in sb doctor.

docs.title: sb add
docs.text:
Nothing is fetched: it queues, like the text mode.

Field Type Meaning queued number Sources newly put in the queue already_known number Sources the queue already had in_wiki list Links not queued because the wiki already has a note for them: {"target", "title"} (the link as given, the note's title)

If any target is invalid, nothing is queued and the output is the error object with bad_target.

docs.title: sb ask
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning answer text The answer, or the refusal ("I find nothing about this in the wiki.", in the notes' language) cited list of text Titles of the pages the answer rests on, without the [[ ]]. Empty when the answer was refused. Titles only: the pages' text is never in the output refused true or false true when no valid citation backed an answer saved text or null With --save and a grounded answer, the path of the saved page relative to the vault (wiki/syntheses/...md); else null unsupported list The sentences the pages do not back: [{"sentence": text, "missing": [text, ...]}], where missing are the numbers and words of the sentence found in none of the pages. In answer those sentences carry a ⚠ and the text ends with a line naming the missing words. Empty when everything is backed, when [run].check_answers = false, or when the pages are in another language than the notes. When most sentences fail the answer is refused (refused: true) and the list still says which. Added without changing contract (1): a reader that does not know it ignores it

A refused answer is a normal object (refused: true, cited: []) with exit 0. Only a failure to ask at all (the model is down, the config is wrong) is an error object, with llm_error or bad_config.

docs.title: sb run
docs.text:
sb run --json prints JSON Lines: one object per event, in this order, each with "contract" and "event". The human progress lines (... chunk 1 of 5, + Note, the summary) are dropped from stdout; warnings stay on stderr.

{"contract": 1, "event": "started", "queued": 2}
{"contract": 1, "event": "source_started", "target": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten", "title": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten"}
{"contract": 1, "event": "step", "target": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten", "name": "chunk", "index": 1, "total": 3}
{"contract": 1, "event": "step", "target": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten", "name": "synthesis"}
{"contract": 1, "event": "source_done", "target": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten", "title": "Zettelkasten", "note": "wiki/sources/Zettelkasten.md"}
{"contract": 1, "event": "source_started", "target": "https://example.com/old", "title": "https://example.com/old"}
{"contract": 1, "event": "source_failed", "target": "https://example.com/old", "attempt": 1, "max_attempts": 3, "parked": false, "reason": "ExtractError: No readable article content found at https://example.com/old"}
{"contract": 1, "event": "finished", "ingested": 1, "failed": 1, "skipped": 0, "tokens": 20826, "stopped_by": null}
event Fields When started queued (number) The queue is about to be drained; how many sources wait. First line source_started target (text), title (text) A source is being read. title is its label (a clip's title, a file name) or else the target step target, name (text), and for chunk and merging section also index and total (numbers) Progress inside a source. name is one of chunk (chunk index of total), merging section (section index of total, only for a source of more than [run].max_chunks chunks), synthesis, detailed summary or connections. A new name can appear later: ignore the ones you do not know source_done target, title, note (text) The source is in the wiki. note is the note's path relative to the vault. Also sent for a source the wiki already had (it is counted as skipped in finished), with the existing note source_failed target, attempt, max_attempts (numbers), parked (true or false), reason (text) A source failed. parked is true when it is out of attempts and waits for sb retry; false when it will be tried again on a later run finished ingested, failed, skipped, tokens (numbers), stopped_by (text or null) Always the last line, whatever ended the run

stopped_by says why the run ended:

Value Means Exit null The queue was drained 0 max_sources --limit or [run].max_sources_per_run was reached; the rest stays queued 0 token_budget [run].max_tokens_per_run was reached; the rest stays queued 0 usd_budget [run].max_usd_per_run was reached (an estimate from [bench.prices]); the rest stays queued, with no attempt counted 0 llm_unavailable The model could not be reached. Nothing is counted against the sources 1 interrupted Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. The source being read went back to the queue with no attempt counted 130 or 143 not_due --if-due and no scheduled batch is due (today's nightly run already happened and nothing is queued, the latest scheduled batch stopped for an outage or an interruption, or [run].max_batches_per_day scheduled batches already ran). This is the only line: no started 0

Other cases:

  • Nothing queued still prints started (with queued: 0) and finished.
  • Another run holds the lock prints one error object with run_in_progress and exits 0: no started, no finished.
  • A config that cannot be used (including a model that cannot be built) prints one error object (config_not_found or bad_config) and exits 1, before any event.
  • A source that fails is not an error object: it is a source_failed event and the run goes on. Only the model being unreachable stops the run, and then the last line is a finished with llm_unavailable.

A reader that wants a status bar needs only started.queued and a count of source_done plus source_failed; one that wants the result reads finished. Read until finished (or an error object), then stop: the process may still be working on the lint and the index, which print nothing on stdout.

docs.title: Inside the vault
docs.text:
~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/        (the vault; its own git repo when git is installed)
├── Home.md              your start page; the worker only edits the block between its two marker comments
├── index.md             catalog of every wiki page (rebuilt by the worker on every run: do not keep your own here)
├── log.md               append-only history: "## [date] ingest | Title"
├── SCHEMA.md            the conventions given to the model
├── inbox/               DROP ZONE: Web Clipper notes, PDFs and images waiting to be picked up (mail attachments land here too)
├── raw/                 originals, never edited
│   ├── inbox/           what arrived through inbox/ or by mail (kept as it came)
│   └── DATE-title-hash.md/.pdf/.png   the text snapshot of each source, with the PDF or image next to it
├── attachments/         figures copied out of PDFs and pictures, one folder per source
├── wiki/
│   ├── sources/         one note per source
│   ├── concepts/  entities/  syntheses/
│   ├── daily/           one index note per day
│   └── review/          things for you: contradiction notes, summaries to review, merge suggestions, Lint.md
├── site/                only if you run `sb export` without --out: the exported website
└── .esbi/               worker state (git-ignored, except golden.jsonl)

docs.title: The state folder, .esbi/
docs.text:
Git-ignored (but for golden.jsonl, which is versioned with the vault), and none of it is in the notes. Delete it to start the worker's memory afresh; the notes are untouched.

File What it is Disposable? queue.sqlite3 The queue: every source, its state, attempts and last error No: it is what remembers what was done index.sqlite3 The page index: names, URLs, hashes, full text, and embeddings when [llm.embed] is set Yes: rebuilt from the vault runs.jsonl One line per sb run: counts, tokens, why it stopped. Feeds the daily note and the nightly due check Yes run.lock The lock that lets only one run work at a time (an flock: a crash cannot leave it stuck) Yes logs/nightly.log Output of the scheduled job; trimmed by itself Yes asks.jsonl One line per sb ask: question, pages retrieved and cited, tokens, seconds Yes golden.jsonl Yours. The questions for sb eval No: it is committed with the vault; without git, back it up bench/ Reports saved by sb bench Yes mail-failed.txt, mail-pdfs.txt Mail the worker could not read (reported once), and fingerprints (hashes) of the PDFs and images that came by mail, so the privacy rules still know a file is email once it sits in inbox/ as a plain file. The file keeps its old name Mostly

docs.title: Page frontmatter
docs.text:
Source note: type: source, title, url, kind (article / paper / email / video), status (processed then read), captured, processed, read (the date you ticked it), tags, summary (one line, used in indexes), raw (path of the original's snapshot), content_hash, format (2 = the rich note; sb reingest rebuilds notes without it), and, for a clip from a site whose page chrome was removed, stripped_lines (how many lines were taken out before reading; absent when none were). The raw snapshot of such a note holds the stripped text, and the clip as it arrived stays in raw/inbox/.

Concept / entity pages: type, title, aliases, tags, sources (links), updated, summary, and, once the page has a consolidated summary, summary_sources (how many sources the page had when that summary was written; the worker compares it with sources to decide when a new summary is due). The body grows one ## From [[source]] section (## Desde in Spanish) per source that mentions it. When a consolidated summary exists, a ## Summary section (## Resumen in Spanish) sits above all the From sections, right under the title: it says what the concept is and what the sources add up to, and the From sections below it are its evidence. It is written by sb consolidate or by the nightly run (see Consolidated summaries); a page without one is as before. Edit it if you like: it is replaced only when a new summary is written.

Synthesis pages (from sb ask --save): type: synthesis, title, question, sources, updated, summary.

Review notes (type: review, in wiki/review/): contradiction notes, Lint.md, and two kinds the consolidated summaries add. They are named after the page and the language of the vault: <page> - summary to review (<page> - resumen por revisar) holds a summary that failed its checks, with the reasons and the proposal (frontmatter kind: summary, and page linking the page); the page itself was not changed. <page> - possible merge (<page> - posible fusión) lists pages that look like the same idea as <page> (kind: merge). Nothing is merged for you: if they are the same, keep one page, add the other's name as an alias, delete the other, then delete the note. Review notes show under To review in the daily index.

Obsidian resolves [[links]] by file name across folders, so the worker never gives a concept the same name as a source or another page.

docs.title: Outside the vault
docs.text:
What Where The settings ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml (or wherever --config or ESBI_CONFIG points; sb info prints it) The mailbox password The macOS Keychain, service esbi-cli-imap, account = your Gmail address The nightly job (macOS) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.esbi-cli.nightly.plist, label com.esbi-cli.nightly The program Homebrew's Cellar, or uv's tool folder (uv tool dir) The models Ollama's own store (ollama list); LM Studio's library

An uninstall touches none of the first two rows: see Update and uninstall.

docs.title: Tutorial: your first week with esbi-cli
docs.text:
You save links and papers. A worker on your Mac reads them, writes notes you can read instead of the originals, connects them to what you already have, and each morning builds an index note to start from. This tutorial walks through one week, one short step a day. Every command is explained in the command reference; here you only learn the habit. If you have not installed it yet, start with Getting started.

Commands are written as sb .... If sb is not found, see Install.

docs.title: What you will have after a week
docs.text:
• A routine: save during the day, read in the morning, tick what you have read.
  • Notes you trust: you know what is in one, what the model may have got wrong, and how to fix it.
  • A wiki that answers questions (sb ask).
  • A nightly job that works without you.

docs.title: Day 0: check the setup
docs.text:
On a brand-new machine, follow Getting started first: it installs sb, runs sb init (which creates the vault and a config file, and asks which kind of model you want) and makes a first note.

sb doctor

Each line says ok, WARN or FAIL, and what to do about it. You want no FAIL. The usual fixes:

Line What it means Fix model summarize: ... is not installed Ollama does not have the model ollama pull llama3.2 Ollama is not reachable Ollama is not running brew services start ollama, or open the Ollama app obsidian: this folder was never opened as a vault Obsidian has not seen the vault Obsidian → Open folder as vault → ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi nightly job: not installed Nothing runs by itself yet Day 4

Open the vault in Obsidian once and look at Home.md. That is your start page.

docs.title: Day 1: put things in
docs.text:
There are two ways to feed it, and you will use both.

A link, from the terminal:

sb add https://example.com/a-good-article

sb add only queues it; nothing is downloaded yet. You can pass several links and .pdf or .md files in one command. A link you already added or already have in the wiki is skipped and says so.

A PDF: drop it into the vault's inbox/ folder (~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/inbox/), or run sb add paper.pdf.

See what is waiting:

sb status

Now process it:

sb run

You will see progress for each source, for example:

  ... chunk 3 of 7
  ... synthesis
  ... detailed summary
  ... connections
  + Attention Is All You Need

What it is doing, in order: reading the source piece by piece (chunk), writing the core note (synthesis), writing the detailed summary (detailed summary), and relating it to your other notes (connections). Expect 3 to 15 minutes per source on a small laptop with a local model; a long paper is on the slow side. This is why the normal way to use it is to let the nightly job do it (Day 4).

sb run does at most 20 sources and stops early if it uses its token budget; what is left stays queued for the next run. sb run --limit 3 does three.

docs.title: Day 2: read a note
docs.text:
sb today

This opens today's index note in Obsidian. Under Processed today you see each new source as a checkbox with a one-line summary. Click a source to open its note. From top to bottom, a note holds:

Section What to do with it Executive summary Two or three sentences. Decide here whether the source deserves your time Detailed summary The argument in order. If you stop here you have not lost the main idea Key ideas Each idea with why it matters Key terms A glossary. A term in a link has its own concept page Key quotes Quotes copied word for word from the source. The worker checks they really are in it Diagram A concept map. Treat it as a hint, not as a fact (see "Trust" below) Figures Figures from a PDF, with their captions Connections to your wiki Other notes of yours this one relates to, with the reason Open questions What the source leaves unanswered Concepts / Entities Pages the note created or added to

When you have read a source, tick its checkbox in the daily note (- [x]). Wait a few seconds for Obsidian to save, then:

sb index

The source becomes status: read and shows up under Read next time. Unticking the box in that day's note (and running sb index) puts the source back to unread.

docs.title: Trust: what can be wrong
docs.text:
The model that writes the notes is small and local, so some things are wrong sometimes:

  • A quote is always real (it is checked against the source). A summary can still be a little off.
  • A glossary term is always in the source. Its definition can be loose, and is sometimes left in English.
  • Connections can be generic ("both talk about attention"). They are suggestions to follow, not findings.
  • The diagram can contain an odd edge.
  • An answer from sb ask cites real pages, and a sentence that says what those pages do not say is marked ⚠. The mark checks words (numbers, names, key words), not meaning, so a sentence that swaps one ordinary word for another can pass: the citation tells you where to read.

When something is wrong, edit the note: it is yours. The worker will not overwrite your edit unless you tell it to (sb reingest, Day 6).

docs.title: Day 3: ask your wiki
docs.text:
sb ask "what is the difference between an agent harness and a prompt?"

It answers only from your notes and cites them. If your notes do not cover it, it says so instead of inventing. A sentence of the answer whose numbers, names or key words are not in the cited pages gets a ⚠ after it and is listed in a line at the end: read it as "check this one" (see the check on the answer). A good answer can be kept as a page of its own:

sb ask "what is the difference between an agent harness and a prompt?" --save

It lands in wiki/syntheses/. Answers are only saved when you ask.

Tip: ask in the words your notes use. By default the search is by keyword, so a question that shares no words with your notes finds nothing; turning on search by meaning fixes most of those. To see how well retrieval works on your notes, use sb eval.

docs.title: Day 4: let it run by itself
docs.text:
Install the nightly job once (this is macOS; on an unsupported system there is no launchd, see Run it every night):

sb schedule install
sb schedule status

It runs sb run every day at 03:00, or at the time you set with nightly_time = "HH:MM" under [run] in config.toml (run sb schedule install again after changing it). If the Mac is asleep, it runs at the next wake. macOS asks once whether Python may read your Documents folder: click Allow. To have the Mac awake at 03:00 (use your own time if you changed it):

sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 03:00:00

(Never earlier than the nightly time; an earlier wake finds nothing due.) Check what it did in the morning: sb status, the Ejecuciones section of the daily note, or ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/.esbi/logs/nightly.log.

The routine now is: during the day sb add or drop PDFs; the night processes them; the morning index is waiting.

docs.title: Day 5: keep it healthy
docs.text:
sb lint

It only reports. If there is anything, it writes wiki/review/Lint.md: broken links, mentions that could be links, possible duplicate pages. Read it, fix what you care about, ignore the rest. Nothing is changed for you.

When a source fails, sb status lists it and the daily note shows it under To review with the last error. A source is tried three times and then parked as failed.

sb retry            # put every parked source back in the queue
sb retry URL        # or just one
sb drop URL         # forget a source for good

Common causes: the page needs a login (clip it with the Web Clipper instead), the page was a blank shell, or the model was off. If the model is off, nothing is lost: sb run stops, keeps the queue, and says so.

docs.title: Day 6: upgrade old notes
docs.text:
When a new version of the worker writes better notes, rebuild the ones you have:

sb reingest                       # every note not yet in the newest format
sb reingest "Attention" "Harness" # only notes whose title contains these words
sb reingest --all                 # everything, again

It rebuilds each note from the original saved in raw/, so it needs no internet. Your read ticks, dates and tags are kept. Before touching anything it tags the vault in git, so one command undoes the whole rebuild:

git -C ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi reset --hard pre-reingest-YYYY-MM-DD

A full rebuild of 24 notes took about 2.5 hours on an 8 GB Mac. If it stops (Mac restarts, Ctrl-C), run sb reingest again and it continues where it stopped.

docs.title: Day 7: what to set up next
docs.text:
• Email: forward articles to a dedicated address and they become notes. Setup is one wizard (sb setup email); see Email.
  • Web Clipper: save pages behind a login and LinkedIn, X or Reddit posts from your browser into inbox/. One wizard: sb setup clipper (see Web Clipper).
  • Models: config.toml sets which model reads and which writes. sb bench compares models on your own notes without touching them.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom First thing to try sb: command not found uv tool update-shell and a new terminal; see Install Nothing happened overnight sb doctor, then read nightly.log. Not due: the nightly run already happened is normal Another run is in progress; skipping A run (or a rebuild) is working; wait for it A run stops with "The LLM is unreachable" Start Ollama. Your queue is intact import esbi_cli fails See Troubleshooting (a macOS hidden-file quirk, source checkouts only) A note looks wrong Edit it, or sb reingest "<part of its title>"

For how it works inside, read Why it is built this way. For one task at a time, see How do I...?.

docs.title: Getting started: from install to your first note
docs.text:
This page takes you from a machine with nothing installed to a first note you can read, one numbered step at a time. Every command is shown with what it prints. Budget about 30 minutes, most of it the model download and the first run.

By the end you will have:

  • sb installed and checked,
  • a model that writes the notes (on your machine, or your Claude subscription, or an API key),
  • a vault with a web page and a PDF turned into notes,
  • the notes open in Obsidian, in any Markdown editor, or as a website,
  • a question answered from your own notes.

Once you have a first note, A first week teaches the daily habit and How do I...? answers any single task.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • A Mac (macOS 13 or later) and a terminal. macOS is the only supported system.
  • About 8 GB of memory for a small local model, and 3 GB of free disk for it. With your Claude subscription or an API key the model runs elsewhere and you need neither.
  • Optional: Obsidian to read the notes. Any Markdown editor works, and sb export makes a website.

Linux and Windows (WSL included) are not supported for now; see the FAQ.

docs.title: Step 1: install sb
docs.text:
Pick one row. They install the same program.

Where Command macOS with Homebrew brew install rubenamaury/esbi-cli/esbi-cli macOS with uv uv tool install git+https://github.com/RubenAmaury/esbi-cli A downloaded wheel (any system with uv) uv tool install ~/Downloads/esbi_cli-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl A copy of the source code git clone https://github.com/RubenAmaury/esbi-cli, then in that folder uv tool install --editable .

Do you not have uv yet? Install it once:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

Open a new terminal afterwards so the command is found. With uv, the install ends like this:

Installed 1 executable: sb

If it adds a warning that the folder "is not on your PATH", run uv tool update-shell and open a new terminal.

Check it:

sb version

0.1.0

Any version number is fine. If you get sb: command not found, see Install. The wheel files are attached to every GitHub release. More detail on every route, and how to update, is in Install.

docs.title: Step 2: get a model
docs.text:
The notes are written by a language model. Choose where it runs. If you are unsure, take A.

Where the model runs What leaves your machine Cost A. Ollama On your machine Nothing Free B. LM Studio On your machine Nothing Free C. Claude subscription At Anthropic, through the official claude tool The text of each source Counts against your plan D. API key At the provider The text of each source Per token

The comparison, and how to change your mind later, is in Choose how the notes are written.

docs.title: A. Ollama (recommended to start)
docs.text:
Install it. On a Mac:

brew install ollama

brew services start ollama

Without Homebrew, follow the installer on ollama.com/download. Check that it is running:

curl http://localhost:11434

Ollama is running

Download the model (about 2 GB, once):

ollama pull llama3.2

The last line it prints is success. Check:

ollama list

NAME                       ID              SIZE      MODIFIED
llama3.2:latest            a80c4f17acd5    2.0 GB    2 minutes ago

docs.title: B. LM Studio
docs.text: Install LM Studio, download a model, load it, and start the local server (Developer tab). Note the model's identifier; lms ls lists it. You will give it to sb init in step 4.

docs.title: C. Claude subscription
docs.text:
Install Claude Code and log in once:

claude auth login

The worker never sees your login: it only runs the claude tool. You will still want a small local model as a fallback and for email, so install Ollama and llama3.2 as in A.

docs.title: D. API key
docs.text:
Put your key in the environment (add the line to your shell profile to keep it):

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"

As with C, install Ollama and llama3.2 for the fallback and for email.

docs.title: Step 3: choose where the notes live
docs.text: The vault is an ordinary folder. sb creates it. A good place is ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi; any folder works. If you use Obsidian, the vault is the folder you open in Obsidian. Do not put it inside a folder that another program rewrites (a git checkout of another project, for example).

docs.title: Step 4: run sb init
docs.text:
sb init

sb init is an installer. Every question has a default, and the first message says so. This is a real run, with the answers that suit most people (Enter takes the default shown in brackets):

esbi-cli turns the PDFs and links you save into a wiki of notes.
That is all you need. Every question below is optional or has a default.

Vault folder [~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi]:
In which language should the notes be written? (The CLI itself is English.)
  1. English
  2. Spanish
Choose [1]: 1
Do you use Obsidian to read your notes? (Any Markdown editor also works) [y/N]: y
How should the notes be written?
  1. On this Mac with a local model (nothing leaves it)
  2. With your Claude subscription (source text goes to Anthropic; email stays local)
  3. With an API key (source text goes to the provider; email stays local)
Choose [1]: 1
Which local runtime? (also used as the failsafe for the other choices)
  1. Ollama (ollama.com)
  2. LM Studio (lmstudio.ai)
Choose [1]: 1
Server address (Enter if it runs on this Mac) []:
Run automatically every night? [y/N]: n
Git remote to back the vault up to (Enter to skip) []:
Read images and scanned PDFs (jpg, png, ...)? It needs a local vision model. [y/N]: n
Vault ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi: inbox/, raw/, attachments/, wiki/sources/, wiki/concepts/, wiki/entities/, wiki/syntheses/, wiki/review/, wiki/daily/, SCHEMA.md, index.md, log.md, .gitignore, git repository
Config ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml: written
Notes language: en (English). The CLI itself is English.
Model: local. Everything stays on this Mac: the notes are written by a local model.

Optional extras (skip both and the app works the same for PDFs and links):
  Connect Gmail, to forward an email and get a note? [y/N]: n
  Set up the Obsidian Web Clipper, to save web pages and YouTube transcripts? [y/N]: n

Next: ollama pull llama3.2, then sb doctor. Add a link with `sb add URL` or drop a PDF in the vault's inbox/ folder.

What each question changes:

Question What your answer changes Vault folder Where the vault is created, and paths.vault in the config. If the folder exists it is kept; only what is missing is added In which language should the notes be written? 1 writes language = "en", 2 writes language = "es": the language of the notes, the daily index and the answers of sb ask. It also writes the vault's SCHEMA.md and index.md in that language. The command line stays English. You can change it later in the config: Language of the notes Do you use Obsidian? y writes viewer = "obsidian": sb today opens an Obsidian link. n writes viewer = "none": sb today prints the path of the note, and the Web Clipper question is skipped (it needs Obsidian) How should the notes be written? 1 writes one local model. 2 writes your subscription as the main model with the local one as fallback, plus a local [llm.private] model for email. 3 does the same with the Anthropic API. It also says what leaves your machine for each Which local runtime? Ollama or LM Studio. This is the local model for 1, and the fallback and email model for 2 and 3. LM Studio asks for the model identifier (lms ls) Server address Only for a local model. Leave it empty when the server runs on this Mac. An address on another machine means the text of your notes goes to that machine; sb init warns, and sb doctor keeps warning Run automatically every night? y asks for a time and installs the nightly job on macOS (elsewhere, which is not supported, it prints a cron line). You can do this later: Run it every night Read images and scanned PDFs? Only with Ollama. The default is No. y shows the vision models with their size and the memory each wants, marks the one that suits this Mac (qwen3-vl:2b-instruct, 1.9 GB, fits 8 GB; deepseek-ocr:3b is for 16 GB or more), lets you type another, and asks Download it now? (default No). It writes an [llm.ocr] section. Change your mind later with sb ocr enable or sb ocr disable Git remote Only shown when git is installed. A remote makes the vault's history a backup; leave it empty to skip. See Back up your vault Connect Gmail / Web Clipper Offers the two guided setups. Skip them now: Capture email and Web Clipper and YouTube cover them later

You can run sb init again at any time. It only creates what is missing and never overwrites your config.

Without questions. Every answer is also a flag, so a script can run sb init with no questions: sb init --vault ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi --model local --language en --no-obsidian. See the command reference. The settings that were written are explained in Configuration.

docs.title: Step 5: check the setup
docs.text:
sb doctor

Each line says ok, WARN or FAIL, and what to do about it. On a fresh install you should see:

  ok   config: ~/.config/esbi-cli/config.toml
  ok   notes language: en (English)
  ok   vault: ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi
  WARN obsidian: this folder was never opened as a vault in Obsidian
         fix: Obsidian > Open folder as vault > ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi
  ok   queue: empty
  WARN last run: no scheduled run yet
         fix: the job does it after the nightly time; or try `sb run --if-due`
  ok   model summarize: ollama/llama3.2:latest is installed
  ok   ocr: off (optional): `sb ocr enable` turns on reading images and scanned PDFs with a local vision model ([llm.ocr], https://rubenamaury.github.io/esbi-cli/docs/reference/configuration/)
  ok   email privacy: all models are local
  ok   email: off (optional)
  WARN nightly job: not installed
         fix: sb schedule install
  ok   global install: ~/.local/bin/sb

You want no FAIL. The warnings above are normal now:

  • obsidian: open the vault once in Obsidian (Open folder as vault, then choose the folder). If you do not use Obsidian you will not see this line.
  • last run and nightly job: nothing has run by itself yet. Both are fixed in Run it every night, whenever you want.

If a line is FAIL, find it in Troubleshooting; the two you are most likely to meet are:

  FAIL model summarize: Ollama is not reachable at http://localhost:11434
         fix: brew services start ollama (or open the Ollama app)
  FAIL model summarize: ollama/llama3.2:latest is not installed
         fix: ollama pull llama3.2:latest

docs.title: Step 6: add your first link
docs.text:
sb add https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zettelkasten

Queued 1 (0 already known). `sb run` processes them.

sb add only queues the link: nothing is downloaded yet. Quote a link that has a ? or & in it, or your shell will try to read it.

docs.title: Step 7: add your first PDF
docs.text:
Copy a PDF into the vault's inbox/ folder (the one you chose in step 4), then ask the worker to look at it:

cp ~/Downloads/paper.pdf ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/inbox/

sb scan

Queued 1 sources from the inbox.

The file has moved to raw/inbox/, where originals are kept and never edited. Look at what is waiting:

sb status

queued: 2
processing: 0
done: 0
failed: 0

You can also do sb add ~/Downloads/paper.pdf instead of copying the file. A scanned PDF or a screenshot needs one more setting, described in Get sources in.

docs.title: Step 8: run it
docs.text:
sb run

The worker fetches each page, reads it in pieces, writes the note, and links it to the notes you already have. This is the real output for the two sources above, a Wikipedia article and a one-page PDF, with llama3.2 on a laptop (about three minutes in all):

    ... chunk 1 of 5
    ... chunk 2 of 5
    ... chunk 3 of 5
    ... chunk 4 of 5
    ... chunk 5 of 5
    ... synthesis
    ... detailed summary
    ... connections
  + Zettelkasten
    ... synthesis
    ... connections
  + Spaced Repetition
ingested: 2, skipped: 0, failed: 0 (20826 tokens)
Lint: 2 issues (see wiki/review/Lint.md)
Wrote wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

What the lines mean:

Line Meaning ... chunk 3 of 5 A long source is read in pieces; this is piece 3 of 5. A short one has none ... synthesis The model writes the core of the note ... detailed summary The detailed summary (long sources only) ... connections The model relates the note to the ones you already have + Zettelkasten A note was written Lint: 2 issues The wiki's health check found two things to look at (not errors)

Expect 3 to 15 minutes per source with a small local model; a long paper is slower. You can stop with Ctrl-C and run sb run again later: what was not finished stays queued (the source that was being read goes back without counting as a failed attempt). If you see The LLM is unreachable (is Ollama running?), start Ollama; nothing is lost.

The notes are in English because you chose English in sb init. Quotes stay in the language of the original. To write in Spanish instead, set language = "es" under [notes]: see Language of the notes.

docs.title: Step 9: read the result
docs.text:
The worker wrote one note per source, pages for the concepts and people it found, and today's index note. Start with the index:

sb today
  • With Obsidian (viewer = "obsidian"), this opens today's index in Obsidian. If Obsidian does not know the vault yet, open the folder once with Open folder as vault.
  • Without Obsidian, it prints the path of the file; open it in any Markdown editor:
~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

The index lists what was processed, as checkboxes:

## Processed today
- [ ] [[Spaced Repetition]] — A learning technique that uses review sessions at increasing intervals to improve memory retention.
- [ ] [[Zettelkasten]] — A system of note-taking and personal knowledge management that consists of small items of information stored on paper slips or cards.

Open a note. A note from a long source has an executive summary, a detailed summary, key ideas, a glossary, verbatim quotes, a diagram, figures, connections to your other notes and open questions. A short source gets a shorter note. This is the real note for the PDF:

## Executive summary
This paper explains the concept of spaced repetition, describes the forgetting curve, and shows how a personal wiki can use review dates to resurface old notes. It concludes that spacing reviews beats cramming and provides a cheap form of spaced repetition with almost no effort.

## Key points
- The forgetting curve: most learned material is forgotten within days unless reviewed
- Scheduling: simple schedules review notes after one day, three days, one week, and one month
- Notes as a system: linking related ideas helps recall, resurfacing old notes provides spaced repetition

## Connections to your wiki
- [[Zettelkasten]]: **complements**. The Zettelkasten system uses notes as a system, linking related ideas to help recall, which is similar to the concept of spaced repetition in the Spaced Repetition paper.

## Concepts
- [[Forgetting Curve]]

When you have read a source, tick its box (- [x]), save, and run:

sb index

Marked 1 source as read.
Wrote wiki/daily/2026-10-03.md

Prefer a website? Make a read-only copy and open it in a browser:

sb export

Exported 8 pages. Open ~/Documents/Obsidian/esbi/site/index.html

More on every part of the note: How a note is made. What each file is: What lives where.

docs.title: Step 10: ask a question
docs.text:
sb ask "What is the forgetting curve and how does it relate to notes?"

The forgetting curve describes the rate at which learned material is forgotten unless reviewed [[Forgetting Curve]]. It suggests that most learned material is forgotten within days unless reviewed.

Sources: [[Spaced Repetition]], [[Forgetting Curve]]

The answer comes only from your notes and cites them. When your notes do not cover the question, it says so instead of inventing an answer:

I find nothing about this in the wiki.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text: What you see Go to sb: command not found Install A FAIL line in sb doctor Troubleshooting The LLM is unreachable (is Ollama running?) Troubleshooting A source that keeps failing Troubleshooting Something not listed Troubleshooting, then open an issue with the output of sb doctor
